entries.how: Seek out SMEs: QC management (coordinates project QC plans and unit QC plan); Safety management (unit safety officer has authority over all safety-related items; each project supervisor designates a crew member as safety representative); Environmental management (advises on environmental, HM, HW issues); Material Liaison Office (MLO) (procurement, tracking, storage of materials; manages project financial records)
entries.wn: The unit safety officer has authority over all safety-related items during the construction process

entries.n: Construction Team and Contracting Office/PW-BOS Support
entries.desc: Understanding roles, responsibilities and authorities of team members is critical to effective communication
entries.use: Know outside organizations that approve or assist with a project
entries.how: Team includes client, contracting office (QA oversight, client liaison, change/design management; USN/USMC = FEAD/ROICC, USA = resident engineer, USAF = base civil engineer), PW/BOS (facilities, utilities, real estate input/approval), architect/engineer (design changes/problems), and base safety, fire, security, environmental departments. Contracting office / PW-BOS support tasks include: final acceptance, material submittals, design change requests, official visitors, schedules up to Level II, material substitutions, QA/QC, technical system assistance, testing plans, turnover and preconstruction meetings, utility outages and communications cutover

entries.n: Receive and Review Construction Directive (Phase 1 Inputs)
entries.desc: Project management does not replace the military planning process or troop-leading procedures
entries.use: Start preliminary planning when a project is tasked
entries.how: Operations officer initiates mission analysis and review of tasking. Essential inputs before Phase 1 planning: construction directive (OPORD/FRAGORD/WARNORD giving who, what, when, where, why), project plans, project specifications. Value-added inputs: unit execution calendar, bill of materials (if available)

entries.desc: The project package is the permanent record of everything that occurs on the project from start to closeout. Appendix A = USN/USA/USMC package; appendix B = USAF package
entries.use: Keep the permanent record of everything that happens on a project
entries.how: Operations maintains the official copy. Project supervisor creates and maintains an on-site project package for the whole project and turns it over to operations for incorporation into the official copy upon completion of construction

entries.n: Determine Task Organization and Project Tasking (Lead/Support Elements)
entries.desc: Sample tasking letter (Figure 2-2) states project, lead/support companies, scope, turnover status and tasked start-stop percent, initial man-day estimate, QC specialist, and due date for the project package
entries.use: Assign who builds the project and who supports it
entries.how: Operations officer does mission analysis, task organization and T/O assignment, then issues a project tasking letter designating lead and support elements. Lead element is responsible for quality, safety and timeliness and directs support elements. Support element is responsible for schedule coordination and resource assignment in sufficient quantity and quality

entries.n: Key Personnel Assignment and Appointment Letters
entries.desc: Sample supervisor appointment letter is effective immediately and expires on completion and acceptance of the project or when transferred at turnover
entries.use: Formally name the project team
entries.how: Designate project manager in writing. Project manager (with chain of command) names project supervisors and crew leaders in writing; an appointment letter outlines duties and responsibilities of each position. Fill the Table of Organization form (project manager, ops chief, supervisor, lead and support crew leaders, safety supervisor, HM/HW rep, QC manager, QC specialist, safety officer, environmental program manager). Project manager assigns planning/estimating staff from both lead and support element crews

entries.n: Project Planning Steps Checklist and Milestones
entries.desc: A milestone represents a decision point, a major accomplishment, or a deliverable. Checklist covers preplanning conference through finalizing the deployment execution plan (e.g., plans/specs review, scope sheet, master activity list, Level II Gantt, long lead items, MTO, BOM compare, logic network, Level III Gantt, 30/60/90-day material lists, CAS sheets, QC/safety/environmental plans, resource leveling, material confirmation, unit and HHQ project briefs)
entries.use: Set the planning timeline and track planning progress
entries.how: Supervisors and crew leaders use the project planning steps checklist (36 line items with primary responsibility) as the primary tool; assign dates to steps as milestones; route the milestones form through the project manager to the operations officer for approval of dates. Use the unit-level project planning flow chart (Phases 1-3) alongside; its reference numbers match the checklist line items
entries.dim: 36 checklist line items

entries.use: Kick off planning with the project team
entries.how: Project manager holds the conference after reviewing the directive to: give overall job approach and construction methods to estimators; identify assumptions and limitations; determine feasibility of a preconstruction site visit; begin monitoring message traffic, SITREPs and correspondence for assigned projects; obtain deployment or project execution calendar

entries.n: Review Plans and Specifications; Project Scope Sheet
entries.desc: If no approved plans/specs exist, HHQ, the tasking authority or supported unit establishes a definitive project scope, enforceable standards and accepted construction practices
entries.use: Understand the work before estimating
entries.how: Project supervisor and crew leaders thoroughly review plans, specs and drawings, read all notes and references, and examine all detail and reference drawings. Then prepare the project scope sheet (title/number, customer, designer, lead element, man-day estimate, BOM source, network duration, status new start/turnover, planned and actual schedule, drawings/specs, permits, points of contact, civil/architectural/mechanical/electrical scope) and forward to the operations officer for approval; once approved, work with estimating staff to build a detailed estimate

entries.n: Review Bill of Materials (BOM) from HHQ
entries.use: Handle a BOM issued by higher headquarters
entries.how: Project manager holds the HHQ BOM until a material takeoff (MTO) and construction estimate are complete, then compares BOM to MTO (para 4.3.3)

entries.use: Close skill gaps before construction starts
entries.how: Project supervisor and crew leaders identify special training and skills needed; submit via project manager to the unit training officer using the Project Training Requirements Plan form (course, justification, rank/name, scheduled, completed)

entries.desc: Figure 2-10 lists 46 example long lead items
entries.use: Flag materials that take a long time to obtain
entries.how: Project supervisor identifies LL items, completes the Long Lead Items form (BOM line, description, intended use, quantity, ROS date required onsite, EOS date estimated onsite), submits to operations officer for review/approval; operations forwards the approved form to MLO, who messages the supported HHQ. Examples list includes air conditioning, circuit breakers, doors, fire alarm and fire protection systems, HVAC components, pre-engineered buildings, structural steel members, transformers, windows, water heaters, treated wood
entries.dim: Note 2: large purchases (more than $10,000 or $25,000 depending on local purchase authority) require time to competitively bid
entries.wn: Finish items such as decorative brick, clay tiles and unusual carpeting may require time to locate; electrical items tend to be unique to each installation and require additional time

entries.desc: Master activities are based on Construction Specifications Institute MasterFormat (effective 2004) divisions, e.g., 03 Concrete, 05 Metals, 06 Wood, 22 Plumbing, 26 Electrical, 31 Earthwork, 32 Exterior Improvements, 33 Utilities
entries.use: Break a project into large functional parts using a standard list
entries.how: Project manager and supervisor determine the master activity (MA) list if HHQ/designer has not. Use the standard MA list (MasterFormat divisions 00-48, Figure 2-13). MAs stay with the project to completion, and MA numbers form the basis for both estimating and scheduling numbering. Supervisor must have the MA list and a narrative project scope before starting a detailed estimate
entries.dim: MA numbers 00-48

entries.use: Make an early rough schedule for planning coordination
entries.how: Supervisor determines rough man-day estimates and durations for each MA, puts them in logical construction sequence, builds a draft Level II Gantt chart and sends it to the operations officer through the project manager for approval

entries.desc: Construction activities are subsets of MAs (definable features of work). A typical military engineer project has between 15-50 construction activities
entries.use: Define the 15-50 definable pieces of work to estimate and schedule
entries.how: Supervisor and crew leaders derive construction activities from the MA list. Each activity is individually estimated for materials, equipment and labor and is tracked for scheduling. Initial list uses columns A and B (number and title); later columns add crew size, total float, baseline duration, estimated man-days
entries.dim: 15-50 construction activities typical

entries.use: Name activities consistently
entries.how: Name each activity as: (1) an action taken, (2) the building element involved, (3) a location identifier. Examples: PREFAB FORMS-FOUNDATION WALL/EAST SIDE; PLACE CONCRETE-FOUNDATION WALL/SOUTH SIDE; ERECT MASONRY WALL-EAST SIDE; INSTALL METAL STUDS-FIRST FLOOR
entries.dim: Action + building element + location

entries.desc: For turnover projects, activity numbers can change but the first two digits remain; only the sequence numeral may change
entries.use: Assign each activity a unique MasterFormat-based number
entries.how: First pair = MA number 00-48; second pair = subcategory 01-99 (Figure 2-17); third pair = sequence number 00-99 for repeated activities, usually assigned in groups of 10. Example: 03 10 10 PREFAB FORMS-FOUNDATION WALL/SOUTH SIDE; 03 10 20 same for EAST SIDE; 03 30 10 PLACE CONCRETE-FOUNDATION WALL/SOUTH SIDE. Project manager assigns numbers after the logic network is complete, to minimize changes. Each activity is documented on a CAS sheet
entries.dim: Digits 1-2: 00-48; digits 3-4: 01-99; digits 5-6: 00-99 (usually by 10s)

entries.n: Construction Work Elements and Work Rates
entries.desc: Example: placing a concrete grade beam direct from chute has a work rate of 0.480 man-hours per cubic yard
entries.use: Break an activity into single-trade tasks for accurate estimating
entries.how: Where more detail is needed, split an activity into work elements (typically one trade/skill), each expressed by a work rate (quantity of time per unit of measure). Take work elements from the data in TM 3-34.41 (Construction Estimating). Work elements get no scheduling number; document them on the associated CAS sheet
entries.dim: Example work rate 0.480 man-hours per cubic yard

entries.use: Confirm preliminary planning is complete
entries.how: Required outputs: project tasking letters; T/O assignments; project planning milestones; project scope sheet; training requirements; long lead items list; master activities list; draft Level II Gantt chart; initial construction activities list. Retain and refine all through planning
entries.dim: 9 required outputs

entries.desc: A Gantt chart is a graphic representation of task duration against time (similar to a synchronization matrix). Used for both planning and monitoring; also provides resource management
entries.use: Show whether a project is ahead of, behind, or on schedule and track actual work-in-place against plan
entries.how: List work activities vertically on the left against a time scale across the top; draw a bar per activity whose start/finish mark the timing and whose length shows duration. Develop it throughout planning and update it throughout execution. Use with a CPM diagram to see relationships between activities, whether an activity is on the critical path, and the effect of an incomplete activity

entries.n: Three Levels of Gantt Charts (Level I, II, III)
entries.desc: The primary difference between levels is the amount of detail
entries.use: Choose the right chart for unit, project, or daily control
entries.how: Level III: one per project; days across the top, construction activities down the side; project supervisors update it daily and plot actual percent complete on the Level II at the end of each two-week period. Level II: weeks across the top for the whole project, master activities down the side with allocated manpower; used for the individual project plan and to control/evaluate progress. Level I: months across the top, individual projects down the side showing total MDs planned and/or expended; primary tool to integrate efforts and manage overall unit tasking (also called synchronization matrix)
entries.dim: Level III = days; Level II = weeks; Level I = months
entries.tm: Level III updated daily; Level II plotted every 2 weeks

entries.desc: MD and man-hour estimates are based on direct labor and do not include allowances for indirect or overhead labor
entries.use: Use one standard unit of labor in all estimates and schedules
entries.how: An MD is a unit of work performed by one person in 8 hours. The MD is a set standard and does not change. The number of hours in a workday may change, but an MD is always 8 hours. Schedules reflect only direct labor (DL) MDs
entries.dim: 1 MD = 8 hours of work by one person
entries.wn: Man-day hours are not the same as workday hours

entries.desc: MDs = Quantity of Work / Unit Size x Man-hours Required per Unit Size / 8 Man-hours per Day
entries.use: Compute man-days needed for a task from material quantity
entries.how: Divide the quantity of work (from the MTO) by the unit size, multiply by man-hours required per unit size, then divide by 8 man-hours per MD. Get production rates from TM 3-34.41
entries.dim: MDs = (Qty / Unit Size) x (MH per Unit Size) / 8

entries.n: Man-Day Capability Computation (MC = DL x WD x ME x AF)
entries.desc: Availability factor (AF) is the amount of time a military engineer is actually on the job. About 20 percent of DL time is lost to leave and liberty, paydays, inspections, quarters, medical and dental, haircuts, military drills, watches and collateral duties. HHQ adjusts AF when accurate timekeeping demonstrates the need
entries.use: Compute total man-day capability of a crew/unit to figure durations or manning
entries.how: MC = DL x WD x ME x AF, where DL = direct labor personnel assigned; WD = available workdays (not calendar days); ME = man-day equivalent, the MDs expended in a typical workday (workday length minus lunch, breaks and travel to/from jobsite, divided by 8); AF = availability factor. HHQ typically directs ME in the construction directive and provides AFs for planning. Also use the equation to find DL manning by substituting tasked MDs for MC
entries.dim: MC = DL x WD x ME x AF. AF ranges 60-90 percent: typical 75 percent main body sites, 80 percent detachment sites, 90 percent contingency construction and theater engagement detachments

entries.n: Activity Duration, Crew Size, AF and ME Equations
entries.desc: Duration changes with AF, crew size and ME. A project supervisor may be able to increase crew size to shorten duration but cannot increase working hours without HHQ approval
entries.use: Solve for duration, crew size, availability factor or man-day equivalent for a construction activity
entries.how: Substitute MD for MC, DUR for WD, CS for DL: MD = CS x DUR x ME x AF. Duration: DUR = MD/(CS x ME x AF). Crew size: CS = MD/(DUR x ME x AF). Availability factor: AF = MD/(CS x DUR x ME). Man-day equivalent: ME = MD/(CS x DUR x AF). Actual crew on an average day = assigned crew x AF. When adjusting durations to resource level, know who controls each factor and which need HHQ approval
entries.dim: MD = CS x DUR x ME x AF; DUR = MD/(CS x ME x AF); CS = MD/(DUR x ME x AF); AF = MD/(CS x DUR x ME); ME = MD/(CS x DUR x AF)
entries.wn: Do not increase length of working hours (ME) without first getting HHQ approval

entries.desc: Example: a multiplier of 1.33 might be applied when using other civilian estimate guides to reflect MDs military engineers need for the same skilled labor. Example: a multiplier of 0.90 when adjusting an estimate based on inclement-weather construction to more favorable weather (10 percent efficiency gain)
entries.use: Adjust a man-day estimate for conditions (e.g., weather, civilian guides, production considerations)
entries.how: Multiply the MD quantity formula by a multiplier/delay factor. 1.0 leaves the estimate unchanged; greater than 1.0 increases MDs; less than 1.0 decreases MDs. Production considerations (eight elements) are in TM 3-34.41
entries.dim: MDs = Qty/Unit Size x MH per Unit Size / 8 x Multiplier; 1.0 = no change; example 1.33; example 0.90

entries.desc: CPM can be used for construction and combat tasks at any level from engineer squad to brigade/regiment. A squad leader should know CPM to understand how assigned tasks affect the total project and, when attached to a maneuver element, to plan, schedule and control personnel, material and equipment
entries.use: Plan, schedule, and control a project using logic network plus precedence diagram
entries.how: CPM comprises two products: a logic network and a precedence diagram. Used together with the Gantt chart it gives the manager all critical information. It requires a formal, detailed investigation of all identifiable tasks, so the manager must envision the project start to finish and estimate time and resources for each task. CPM schedule development involves continual refinement as decisions are made and changes incorporated

entries.desc: Services use CPM similarly but with differing procedures; appendixes C and D present alternate CPM procedures
entries.use: Know what CPM does and does not do for you
entries.how: CPM does not make decisions or contribute anything tangible to construction. Advantages: reduces risk of overlooking essential tasks and gives a long-range blueprint; shows logical relationships (helpful for a new manager); draws attention to critical tasks; gives information for rational timely decisions; shows resources needed and availability timeline; shows quickly what extra resources are needed to finish early; provides feedback on a finished project for future projects
entries.wn: CPM is not a cure-all for engineer problems

entries.desc: Example: Prefab Forms and Set Rebar cannot start until Move-in completes; Set Forms cannot start until Prefab Forms completes; Place Concrete cannot start until Set Rebar and Set Forms complete
entries.use: Show activity sequence and interdependencies so no work item is overlooked
entries.how: Supervisor and crew leaders build it from the initial construction activities list. Durations and crew sizes are immaterial at this stage; identify all required activities, sequence, and relationships. Recommended technique: label pieces of paper with each activity name, place labels in construction sequence on a roll of paper, tape in place, and draw dependencies. Then assign activity numbers and produce the initial construction activities list. Each activity is a rectangle (node); arrows show relationships
entries.eq: Paper labels, roll of paper, tape (recommended technique)

entries.desc: The critical path is the group of construction activities that must be started on time and completed within the duration to finish by the scheduled completion date. USA/USMC version of the activity block is in appendices C and D
entries.use: Show overall project duration and identify the critical path
entries.how: Inputs: numbered activity list, logic network diagram, summary of activity durations (from CAS sheets). Each logic network node becomes an activity block holding the numbers needed for forward/backward pass. Event-time numbers represent the END of the time period (start or finish of day 5 = end of fifth day or beginning of sixth). Update the time analysis whenever estimates change
entries.wn: A time analysis based on outdated estimates is useless

entries.n: CPM Forward Pass (Early Start / Early Finish)
entries.desc: Lag times are mandatory wait times between activities (e.g., concrete cure time before stripping forms)
entries.use: Find earliest start and finish days for each activity
entries.how: Start with the first activity: ES = 0. Add duration to get EF. EF plus lag (if any) becomes ES of the next activity. With two or more predecessors, use the larger EF plus lag
entries.dim: ES + DUR = EF; EF + Lag = ES (next activity); use larger EF + lag when 2+ predecessors
entries.wn: Numbers are rounded up; not all software rounds, which may create different outcomes

entries.n: CPM Backward Pass (Late Start / Late Finish)
entries.use: Find latest start and finish days that do not delay the project
entries.how: Start with the last activity: LF = EF. Subtract duration to get LS. LS minus lag (if any) becomes LF of the preceding activity. With two or more successors, use the smaller LS minus lag
entries.dim: LF - DUR = LS; LS - Lag = LF (preceding activity); use smaller LS - lag when 2+ successors
entries.wn: Numbers are rounded up; not all software rounds, which may create different outcomes

entries.desc: A critical activity, if delayed any amount, delays the entire project by the same amount. Float is extra time available to complete an activity beyond its duration (e.g., 6 days available for 4 days of work). No critical-path activities have float
entries.use: Identify the activities that cannot slip
entries.how: An activity is critical if: ES = LS; EF = LF; and ES (or LS) + duration = EF (or LF). Linked critical activities form the critical path from start to finish. Mark it with double slash lines, bold lines, or highlighted color. Every other activity has float. A precedence diagram always has at least one critical path; critical paths may branch and rejoin
entries.dim: Critical: ES=LS, EF=LF, ES/LS + DUR = EF/LF
entries.wn: Any critical path that does not begin at the start node and end at the finish node indicates a logic mistake

entries.desc: Total float is the number of days an activity can be delayed without delaying the project completion date
entries.use: Find how many days an activity can slip without delaying project completion
entries.how: Compute TF = LS - ES or LF - EF; do both to check for math errors. Example: activity 03 10 00 could finish as early as day 10 or as late as day 12, so TF = 2 days
entries.dim: TF = LS - ES or LF - EF

entries.desc: Free float is the number of days an activity can be delayed without delaying the ES date of the follow-on activity
entries.use: Find how many days an activity can slip without reducing the float of its follow-on activity
entries.how: FF = ES (next activity) - Lag (if any) - EF; with two or more successors use the smaller result. Always uses early days. Example: ES of 03 10 10 (11) - lag 0 - EF of 03 10 00 (10) = 1 day FF. Delaying 2 days pushes the successor start and reduces the first activity's float to zero; delaying more than 2 days (its TF) delays the project
entries.dim: FF = ES(next) - Lag - EF

entries.n: Logic Types (FS, SS, FF, SF) and Schedule Compression
entries.desc: Start-to-start equations: ES + DUR = EF; ES + Lag = ES (next); LF - DUR = LS; LS - Lag = LS (preceding); FF = ES(next) - Lag - ES. Finish-to-finish equations: ES + DUR = EF; EF + Lag = EF (next); LF - DUR = LS; LF - Lag = LF (preceding); FF = EF(next) - Lag - EF. TF = LS - ES or LF - EF for both
entries.use: Choose how activities depend on each other; compress a late schedule
entries.how: Finish-to-start (most common): an activity must finish before the next can start; gives longest project duration. Start-to-start: start of second depends on start of first. Finish-to-finish: finish of second depends on finish of first. Start-to-finish: second cannot complete until first starts (e.g., cannot cut off temporary power until permanent electrical system is turned on). Use start-to-start and finish-to-finish to compress (shorten) the schedule during execution to catch up, and for repetitive projects such as roadway or pipeline construction
entries.dim: SS: ES+Lag=ES(next), FF=ES(next)-Lag-ES; FF-type: EF+Lag=EF(next), FF=EF(next)-Lag-EF

entries.n: Level III Gantt Chart (Early Start Schedule)
entries.desc: If the activity starts on its ES date, actual and baseline starts stay in place; if earlier or later, the piston slides to the actual start date
entries.use: Build the day-to-day activity schedule from the precedence diagram
entries.how: List each construction activity in order of ES date; mark each activity's timeframe (scheduling on earliest day yields the early-start Level III). A bar shows start date, finish date and duration. Set baseline start/finish before the activity starts; a 'piston' inside the bar shows actual start and forecast finish and is shaded to show percent complete / WIP; a series of dots after the bar represents total float. May be drawn by hand or software

entries.use: Compare daily resource requirements to available resources
entries.how: Add a histogram to the bottom of the Level III Gantt chart (manually or by software). Line items are labor categories, equipment and any constrained item; list required totals for each day by column, each resource computed separately. When requirements exceed available resources (example crew size seven), delay selected activities using float to spread requirements

entries.desc: Resource leveling shifts activity schedules to spread requirements across the project timeframe while avoiding overall project delay. Information comes from the precedence diagram, CAS sheets, and an activity summary sheet (CS, TF, baseline duration, estimated MDs). Example: a 1-day-float activity that moves 1 day becomes critical; moving more than 1 day extends the project
entries.use: Spread labor/equipment demand to fit available crew without delaying the project
entries.how: Goals: keep troops gainfully employed every day and keep work on schedule. Start by identifying daily critical-path labor requirements. Working top to bottom: (1) find the activity with the least total float; (2) find the first dates with available resources; (3) mark the dates to schedule the activity; (4) update the histogram. Schedule delayed noncritical activities on days when total resources required are below crew size. Consult the precedence network before moving an activity, since successors must move at least the same amount. Then determine crew rate/trade makeup and enter final dates in software
entries.dim: Example crew of seven
entries.wn: Do not move activities unless necessary. Rescheduling may create additional critical activities and less float. Do not leave impractical gaps (example: an excavated septic hole sitting empty for 2 weeks)

entries.n: Develop Level II Gantt Chart (7 Steps)
entries.desc: Example: activity 03 10 30 = 5 MDs over 4 days with 1 nonworkday = 3 days; 5/3 = 1.67 MDs per day; 2 days = 3.34, 1 day = 1.67; rounded 3 + 2 = 5. Example project total 452 MDs; MA 03 = 140 MDs = 31 percent (rounded down to 30 so column totals 100)
entries.use: Roll the resource-leveled Level III up to a master-activity weekly/biweekly chart with a percent complete curve
entries.how: Step 1: from Level III, compute estimated MDs per reporting period (normally 1 week) by master activity; prorate MDs across split weeks, subtracting nonworkdays. Step 2: transfer MDs per period for each MA. Step 3: total MDs for each MA into the MDs Tasked column. Step 4: total the MDs Tasked column for the project total. Step 5: weighted percent by MA = MA MDs / total project MDs x 100; column must total 100 (adjust the highest). Step 6: total MDs scheduled per two-week period and cumulative; last cumulative must equal project total. Step 7: scheduled percent complete = cumulative MDs / total project MDs x 100; plot a dot at end of each two-week period and connect the dots
entries.dim: Weighted % = MA MDs / Project MDs x 100 (total must = 100); Scheduled % complete = Cumulative MDs / Total MDs x 100; Level II columns = last workday of every two-week period
entries.wn: If cumulative total does not equal project MD total, recalculate for a math error

entries.n: Level I Gantt Chart / Synchronization Matrix
entries.use: Integrate and manage overall unit tasking across all projects
entries.how: Project manager builds it like the Level II, using Level II charts and project SITREPs. Months across the top; individual projects down the side with total MDs planned and/or expended. Figures show unconstrained version and two resource-leveling attempts

entries.desc: Phase 2 ends upon project package consolidation and readiness for the approval process
entries.use: Check you have what you need before detailed planning
entries.how: Essential inputs: construction directive (with commander's intent), project plans, project specifications, unit execution calendar, table of organization, project planning milestones, submittal register. Value-added: BOM (if available), tasking letters, scope sheet, master activities list, training requirements plan, long lead list, draft Level II Gantt, initial construction activities list. Plan around two questions: how to accomplish the tasking, and what is needed to do it

entries.desc: If a visit is not feasible, mitigate unknowns by following through on RFIs, conducting map searches, and contacting on-site personnel
entries.use: Verify existing conditions against site plans and answer planning questions
entries.how: Project supervisor documents information requirements and assumptions as a checklist for the site visitor. Complete the Project Site Visit Summary (status new start/turnover; for turnover: differences between observed and reported status, obtain on-site unit's project package and management tools, submittal status, whether material returns to MLO; missing plans/specs/BOM; local forms; permits - excavation, utility outage, burning, hauling; percent of materials on hand and expected at turnover; special skills). A unit or HHQ project manager often does the visit; include supervisors and sometimes crew leaders if time allows. Prepare a sketch of the site and compare to the site plan; consider orientation and space for materials and equipment

entries.desc: Estimating itself is covered in TM 3-34.41
entries.use: Determine materials, equipment, labor and methods for each activity
entries.how: Break the project into sequenced construction activities; estimators produce detailed material, equipment, and labor estimates per activity and summarize into a project estimate; create shop drawings as required. Supervisor and crew leaders decide construction methods or document assumptions, since method affects materials, equipment, tools, safety gear and labor. Estimating worksheets become part of the project package and feed the CAS sheets

entries.n: Bill of Materials (BOM) and BOM/MTO Comparison
entries.desc: Add-on/reorder justification routing includes lead company projects chief, QC specialist, MLO (excess available? funds available?), QC manager, and operations officer approval
entries.use: Make sure the official material list is complete and correct
entries.how: BOM is the official record of project material requirements and includes construction materials, equipment rental/purchase of special tools and safety items not organic to the TOA/table of equipment, and subcontractors or contracted technical assistance (e.g., balancing an HVAC system, certifying a fire alarm). Three steps: (1) compare original BOM to MTO using the BOM/MTO comparison worksheet; (2) document and justify added items on the add-on/reorder justification form and route to the operations officer per SOP; (3) operations officer approves and submits to logistics on the BOM add-on/reorder form
entries.wn: Verify an HHQ-supplied BOM has everything required in the correct quantities per the MTO

entries.n: Develop Precedence Diagram and Level III Gantt (Detailed Planning)
entries.use: Turn the logic network and labor estimate into a working schedule
entries.how: Supervisor builds the logic network from the initial activities list, identifies interdependencies, then builds the precedence diagram using duration and crew size from the labor estimate (MD = CS x DUR x ME x AF). Then builds the Level III Gantt chart: in planning it resource-levels to constrained resources, compresses the schedule to a desired completion date, or justifies additional resources; in execution it becomes the primary daily scheduling tool for labor, equipment, inspections and material deliveries

entries.desc: Submit the list through the chain of command to the operations officer for review no later than 2 1/2 months before project start. Operations forwards it to the supporting logistics organization and copies the HHQ project support office no later than 2 months before project start
entries.use: Tell logistics what material is needed in the first 3 months
entries.how: Supervisor identifies materials by BOM line item number needed in the first 30, 60 and 90 days using the Level III Gantt chart, CAS sheets and estimating worksheets. Form columns: MTO/BOM number, line item number, description, quantity, unit of issue, RDD (required delivery date), status. Circle whether 30-, 60-, or 90-day list
entries.dim: Submit to ops: no later than 2 1/2 months before start; ops to logistics/HHQ: no later than 2 months before start

entries.desc: See para 9.4.11 for submittal procedures
entries.use: Provide manufacturer and construction-method information for approval
entries.how: Provide submittals as directed by the project manager and QC manager. A submittal includes manufacturer's information, shop drawings, samples, other descriptive literature, information for required materials, and construction methods and plans used in execution. Keep a submittal register and status log

entries.desc: Labor histograms go to unit operations via the lead element project manager for unit-wide resource leveling. Tools/equipment are consolidated on tool and equipment requirement summary forms; if organic items are not available, rent from commercial vendors if project funds are sufficient and list any expenditure on the BOM
entries.use: Central depository of everything about one construction activity; drives scheduling and execution
entries.how: Created by project supervisor and crew leaders after the unit approves the activity list; CAS titles/numbers parallel the activity names/numbers. Form holds: master activity number, baseline/actual start and finish, estimated/actual duration and man-days, availability factor, man-day equivalent, description of work, method of construction/assumptions, work elements (reference table/code, unit of measure, quantity, delay factor/multiplier), labor resources (rate, skill, qty), tool/equipment resources, material resources (BOM line item, unit of issue, qty, long lead Y/N), QC plan (requirement, spec reference, control measure), safety plan (hazard, reference, RAC, control measure), environmental plan (hazard, reference, action required). Document assumptions, MD/duration/tool/equipment calculations, notes and significant events; attach additional pages to the back. Add the scheduled start/finish from the Level III Gantt chart

entries.use: Consolidate tools and equipment needed across activities
entries.how: Tool Requirement Summary columns: activity number, tool requirement, non-TOA, TOA, dates required. Equipment Requirement Summary columns: construction activity, equipment required, qty, start, finish, operator required?. Forward both through the lead element project manager to unit operations for unit-wide resource leveling

entries.n: Plan QC, Safety and Environmental Requirements During Planning
entries.use: Build hazard and quality controls into the plan from the start
entries.how: Supervisor and crew leaders identify hazards, requirements, and corrective actions during estimating and annotate the applicable CAS sheet; consolidate summary plans from CAS sheets when planning is complete. The unit QC manager/QC specialist prepare an independent QC plan for comparison, identify and resolve differences. Unit safety and environmental SMEs review plans before project manager approval

entries.n: Master Activity Summary Sheet and Level II Baseline
entries.use: Roll up resources by master activity and set the baseline for measuring progress
entries.how: After the Level III and CAS sheets are final, consolidate CAS sheets of like master activities into Master Activity Summary Sheets (activities, crew size, duration, man-days, labor and equipment resources, assumptions) to manage resources at company and unit level. Derive the Level II Gantt from the resource-leveled Level III; it establishes the scheduled progress curve and baseline for measuring progress

entries.use: Confirm detailed planning is complete
entries.how: Required outputs: site visit summary; construction estimate; shop drawings (as required); BOM; BOM add-on/reorder; precedence diagram; Level III Gantt; 30/60/90-day material list; submittals and status log; CAS sheets; QC plan; safety plan; environmental protection plan; tool requirement summary; equipment requirement summary; master activity summary sheet; Level II Gantt
entries.dim: 17 required outputs

entries.n: Compile and Sign Off Project Package
entries.use: Get the package approved before mobilizing
entries.how: Supervisor consolidates and checks the package for completeness and sends it through the chain of command to the unit operations officer. Include a cover sheet 'Project Package Sign-off Sheet' with project number/title and columns Reviewed By (Title), Name (Signature), Date. Minimum reviewers: support element crew leader(s), project supervisor, company operations chief, project manager, QC approving authority, safety program approving authority, environmental program approving authority, unit operations officer
entries.dim: 8 minimum reviewers

entries.use: Fit all projects to available tools, equipment and labor
entries.how: Project managers consolidate resource requirements per project and for all projects (spreadsheets/software per SOP), resource-level them, identify shortfalls, then decide whether to request more resources or prioritize available assets, and adjust the plan

entries.n: Readiness to Deploy / Management Assist Visit Checklist
entries.desc: Checklist may also be used by supervisors to prepare for readiness evaluations and management assist visits
entries.use: Verify the project package, deployment plan, files, crew, safety and equipment before deploying or during a visit
entries.how: Project package review items include: construction logic; complete five-section package; CAS sheets match Level III; Level III matches Level II; QC and safety plans match back of CAS sheets; crew size matches Level III; Level II lines up with deployment schedule; MTO compared with BOM and add-ons prepared; 30/60/90-day message sent; special tools/equipment identified; contract support identified; funding known; safety items complete; documented contact with on-site unit on safety; lockout/tagout and temporary power personnel named in writing. Deployment plan: manning, direct labor capability vs plan, Level I matches Level II and deployment calendar. Site visit: project sign current; CAS sheets, Level II, Level III and two-week schedule posted and updated; QC and safety reports available; material receipt file current; plans/specs with changes annotated; MSDS and HM inventory; supervisor knows material delays, subcontractor schedule, QC problems, pending FARs/DCDs; crew size in line; safety (power tools/cords checked, temporary power certified, generators grounded, eyewash, clean water jugs, first aid kits, fire extinguishers, rebar caps, PPE); equipment (daily inspection, prestart, operating checks, clean, operator maintenance)

entries.n: Material Procurement Status and On-Site Unit Procurement Percentages
entries.desc: Failure of the on-site unit to procure adequate material may cause project delays
entries.use: Make sure materials are procured for new starts and turnover projects
entries.how: Supervisor knows required materials for critical-path activities and when needed; submits material requisitions and the 30/60/90-day list to start the procurement cycle. The on-site unit procures materials for both new-start and turnover projects tasked to the relieving unit. Prior to arrival of the relieving unit's advance party the on-site unit must have on hand 100 percent of the first 30- and 60-day material, 80 percent of the 90-day material, and 80 percent of all remaining materials
entries.dim: 100% of first 30 and 60 days; 80% of 90 days; 80% of all remaining materials (before relieving unit advance party arrives)

entries.desc: Sample brief in appendix E
entries.use: Show the commander/HHQ you understand and can execute the project
entries.how: Given twice: (1) Preconstruction confirmation brief by the project supervisor and crew leaders to the commander's/HHQ representative to demonstrate understanding of commander's intent, tasks, purpose and relation to the operational environment (reveals plan gaps and resource discrepancies). (2) In-process review by HHQ focusing on progress to date versus planned estimate and schedule, and justification for any man-day tasking changes. Follow unit SOP; generally modify the five-paragraph order format

entries.desc: Persons outside the engineer community see engineers, not separate units
entries.use: Hand off or accept a project without hurting the unit's reputation
entries.how: Project supervisor plans and conducts the turnover per the operations officer's policy on behavior, schedules and expectations. Set the example for professionalism. Outgoing unit sets up the incoming unit for a successful start; relieving unit protects the reputation of the outgoing unit
entries.wn: It is unprofessional to criticize another unit; blaming a previous unit for quality or timeliness problems makes engineers look unprofessional

entries.n: Project Status at Turnover SITREP and Turnover Checklist
entries.use: Report exactly what remains on each project at turnover
entries.how: On-site unit sends HHQ and the relieving unit a Project Status at Turnover SITREP 60 days before redeployment. It lists each project's number, title, projected WIP percent at turnover, man-days remaining (horizontal/vertical), summary comments, and projected WIP by master activity. Use the Project Turnover Questions Checklist: annotated schedule, scope sheets for remaining activities, contracting office approval of WIP, complete project file (as-builts, QC/safety plans, QC reports, vendor submittals, O&M manuals, change orders, manpower record, correspondence, fabrication drawings, specs, photos), material info (MTO and addendum, BOM worksheets, annotated MTO, status reports, requisition follow-up, shelf-life list, HM list), funds status, tools bought with project funds, monitoring tools, lessons learned, method improvements, incomplete electrical systems tagged, circuits/conduits/piping labeled, percent complete
entries.dim: SITREP due 60 days before redeployment

entries.desc: For turnover projects and new-start repair/alteration projects, the on-site unit must procure and provide 100 percent of local purchase materials. For new-start construction projects it must have on hand 50 percent of local purchase materials
entries.use: Check quantity, quality and condition of material at turnover
entries.how: Project supervisor is responsible for all material turned over on site and arranges with MLO staff to inspect project materials held at MLO; check quantity, quality, type and condition even though MLO counts it. On-site unit submits a monthly local material procurement status SITREP; relieving-unit planners monitor it plus the project material status report
entries.dim: 100% local purchase material (turnover and repair/alteration new starts); 50% (new-start construction)

entries.n: Turnover Memorandum Worksheet and Percent Complete at Turnover
entries.desc: Funding contingency = (pipeline costs + future funding requirements) x 10 percent; Total costs = actual expenditure + pipeline + future requirements; Estimate at completion = total costs + contingency. New MD completion estimate = 6b + 6c + 6d; MDs expended total = 6b + 6c
entries.use: Document conditions and decisions at turnover and agree on remaining man-days
entries.how: Relieving unit operations officer ensures all project files are current before accepting. Lead elements use the Turnover Memorandum Worksheet: contacts, scope, work completed by master activity from physical observation, rework (WIP not conforming to plans/specs), work remaining, labor statistics (MD estimate, MDs expended, remaining MDs by rate and master activity, percent complete based on WIP), project files, engineering, construction company, material status, funding status, tools, lessons learned, contracting office punch list. Percent complete focuses on MDs of work remaining: the two units and contracting office review estimates by activity until they agree on total MDs remaining; if they disagree whether WIP conforms to plans/specs, consult the contracting office. All participants get a copy plus the project file
entries.dim: Rework more than 50 MDs or $500 in materials requires HHQ approval. Funding contingency = (pipeline + future funding) x 10%
entries.wn: Any rework estimated to require more than 50 MDs or $500 in materials requires approval of HHQ

entries.use: Keep reported progress consistent across units
entries.how: The project WIP curve must be continuous unless HHQ issues an approved scope change. To revise previously reported WIP, submit a message request with justification to HHQ; this includes downward adjustments during turnover negotiations. Any downward adjustment in the turnover SITREP must be explained. After turnover, the relieving unit cannot reduce previously reported WIP without justification to HHQ

entries.use: Formally hand over each turnover project
entries.how: Outgoing unit schedules the conference and invites the same attendees as the preconstruction conference. Contracting office prepares minutes (including decisions), signed by engineering unit representatives and COTR, and placed in the project file. Operations officers give subordinates guidance on interaction with the contracting office, COTR, local personnel and contractors; weekly meetings between the operations officer and the contracting office/COTR usually eliminate problems
entries.dim: Weekly ops/contracting office meetings

entries.desc: Summary form notes: client-initiated scope changes go to the contracting office via DCDs and must be approved before execution; approved FARs and DCDs are the only authorized means of changing plans/specs; engineering updates plans/specs on receipt of approved FARs/DCDs. Also records permits (site approval, excavation, tree removal), O&M manuals, submittals, client-supplied materials, utility outages, security clearances, prefab yard, environmental protection
entries.use: Get the notice to proceed from the contracting office
entries.how: Hold before work starts on a new start or resumption of a hold project. Present methods per plans, specifications and QC procedures; if the contracting office is convinced the unit is prepared to meet the schedule, it issues a notice to proceed (approving QC and safety plans with changes). Typical attendees: contracting office, COTR, operations officer/assistant/chief, company commander(s)/detachment OIC, subcontractor reps, project supervisors and crew leaders, project QC rep, project safety rep, customer reps. Prepare with the 33-question unit preparation checklist (e.g., unanswered plan/spec questions, field conditions, vendor submittals, materials by line item, MTOs, QC/safety plans approved, equipment/tools, network schedule, excavation permits, utility outages, temporary utilities, working hours, after-hours POC, base security, off-site prefab, reporting requirements, environmental plans). Lead element takes minutes on the Preconstruction Conference Summary form and gives copies to all attendees and the project file
entries.dim: 33 checklist questions
entries.wn: The notice to proceed may be canceled if the project is not executed in accordance with the plans presented

entries.use: Confirm final planning and turnover/mobilization are complete
entries.how: Required outputs: complete project package; unit Level I Gantt chart; unit deployment execution plan per SOP; project turnover completed (turnover SITREP and turnover memorandum); mobilization completed (preconstruction conference summary)
entries.dim: 5 required outputs

entries.n: Jobsite Layout Objectives and Organization Checklist
entries.desc: Good organization raises productivity, reduces loss/pilferage/damage/deterioration of staged materials, makes a safer site, and frees the supervisor from minor production decisions
entries.use: Set up the jobsite for productivity, safety and control
entries.how: Supervisors submit jobsite requirements through the chain of command to the contracting office and prepare a layout sketch of area limits showing impact on adjacent buildings, sites and personnel and the lay-down areas. Layout objectives: unimpeded work flow; shortest simplest transport paths; safeguard resources; efficient receiving/inventory/staging; supervisor can monitor and control (visibility, access, ease of inspection); operational flexibility from rough/heavy trades to finishing trades; adjust to site constraints (weather, terrain, scope/class of work, interferences). Organization checklist covers traffic/work flow and congestion, prefab yard spaces, materials staging and storage (store by trade; first-used/last-used locations; palletized, stacked, sheltered, raised off ground; drainage; aisle and loader access; protection against deterioration, handling, theft; box trailers for small valuable parts; mats/platforms for heavy loads on soft ground), equipment and maintenance site location (parking, maintenance pads, POL storage, fueling, dust control, batch plants), haul roads and pits (minimum climb, minimum haul time, minimum downshifts, rolling resistance, drainage, maintenance), temporary utilities (power and lighting, water, potable water, toilets, storm drainage, fire lines, fuel, office, bulletin boards, survey benchmarks, watchman shack, borrow pits), security and safety (gates, fences, locked storage, barricades, safety lights, watchman)

entries.n: Jobsite Appearance, Field Office and Project Sign
entries.use: Keep the site clean, safe and professional
entries.how: Crew picks up after themselves during the day and does a final cleanup at day's end; trash in receptacles. Store materials neatly out of the way and out of weather; dispose of unusable/damaged materials quickly. Erect a professional project sign (watch for misspelled names) and an organized field office. Keep safety precautions in place at all times (open excavations, fall protection, vehicle traffic, hygiene, electrical setups). Project sign is built by the project crew per unit SOP and shows current project supervisor and safety supervisor names. Field office may be an equipment shelter or other structure separate from tool and material storage
entries.wn: Never use project materials to construct a field office or build anything in it unless project funds stipulate material purchase for that purpose

entries.use: Daily reminder to keep jobsite and project documents current
entries.how: Housekeeping: containers/offices/tool kits neat; excess material removed; lumber free of protruding nails and scrap metal; professional current project sign; vehicles clean and prestarted. Crew: assistant project supervisor designated; crew knows next assignments if project finishes early; knows CAS sheet info for next several activities, timekeeping, QC inspector, project safety supervisor; hard hats and steel-toed boots at all times; strict adherence to daily routine; unit integrity maintained as much as possible. Project management: as-built (redline) drawings current and on project; specs annotated; BOM reflects material status; kit inventories current; logbook current; information board current; crew briefings conducted and documented; QC, safety and environmental plans current; Level III and Level II reflect actual status; CAS sheets reflect Level III progress, actual dates and BOM/tool/equipment status; two-week schedule reflects actual status; project package complete; two-week labor summary up to date
entries.wn: Hard hats and steel-toed boots must be worn at all times

entries.desc: Board is the focal point of the project package information; the package is protected and kept organized until project completion, when it is finalized and turned in to the unit QC office
entries.use: Communicate project status to crew and visitors
entries.how: Project supervisor owns and updates the board daily; boards should be the same throughout the unit (content per unit/HHQ SOP). If an item is too large to display (Level III Gantt chart, large MSDS binder), note its location in the field office. Post emergency phone numbers on all project sites: medical/ambulance, fire department, hospital, base security, explosive ordnance disposal, operations, safety officer, mishap investigator, quarterdeck, building number/project site, nearest telephone, environmental manager, spill response emergency notification

entries.use: Tell the crew what, how, how long, how well and how safely each day
entries.how: Daily production briefing: activity to perform, how, how much time is scheduled, how a delay impacts overall schedule. Quality control measures: that day's QC measures and expected quality level. Stand-up safety lecture: activity's safety hazards and preventive measures (use preparatory/initial phase checklists in 9.5.1 and 9.5.2); record on the daily safety lecture log

entries.desc: Fire extinguishers: one for every 3,000 square feet (or major fraction) of building space; travel distance from any point to nearest extinguisher not to exceed 100 feet. First aid kits checked weekly. Warning signs: red for immediate hazards, yellow for potential hazards
entries.use: Make sure the mandatory safety items are on every jobsite
entries.how: Required: communication/transportation for rapid mishap response; drinking water from approved source labeled for drinking only (no common cups); posted emergency plans with nearest phone and numbers for ambulance, hospital, physician, police, fire; eyewash where handling poisons, acids, caustics, toxic chemicals; fire extinguishers; first aid kits readily available and checked weekly for consumed items; first-aid-qualified crew member on site if medical facility not readily accessible; hazardous material inventory sheet and MSDS for any HM on site; safety and health manuals (29 CFR 1926, EM 385-1-1 or as directed by HHQ SOP); temporary fencing/barricades in actively used public areas; portable toilets if none available; warning signs
entries.dim: Fire extinguisher: 1 per 3,000 sq ft; max travel 100 ft. First aid kit check: weekly. Red sign = immediate hazard; yellow = potential hazard

entries.use: Periodic site checks to eliminate safety violations
entries.how: Check: floor openings/trenches barricaded or covered; rebar ends covered; wheels chocked on required vehicles; clean drinking water with cups; crew knows closest medical facility; daily safety lecture given; emergency response plan known, assets available, rehearsed by crew; dedicated fire extinguisher for hot work; extinguishers staged and checked within the last month; flag person/back-up guides where vehicle traffic is a danger; GFCIs/spider boxes on all temporary power; loose materials secured against high winds; overhead utilities secured before scaffold erection and work near power lines; eye/face and hearing protection and PPE; hot-work protective clothing; power sources tagged with recertification every 2 weeks; power tools and cords visually inspected before use; site roped off; scaffolding handrails, toe boards, bracing; underground utilities marked by dig safe authority, secured and hand-located before machine excavation; vehicle available to transport injured; warning signs posted (e.g., hard hat area); welders or light plants not used as power source
entries.dim: Power source tag recertification every 2 weeks; fire extinguishers checked within last month
entries.wn: Hand-locate and mark underground utilities before machine excavation begins. Do not use welders or light plants as a power source

entries.desc: Sample page shows arrival/departure times, visitors, QC/safety concerns, end-of-day progress table (activity, total work, work complete, percent), material received, equipment on-site, and man-hours by activity code
entries.use: Record daily events so project status can be assessed and documents updated later
entries.how: Project supervisor writes down events and actions before they are forgotten. Record: date, weather, and timeline of daily events; end-of-day progress of WIP for in-progress activities (quantity complete vs total work, percent WIP); material received; equipment on the jobsite; timecard notes (man-hours by activity code and by crew rate). Also keep a damaged-materials record

entries.desc: Manual example: concrete request scheduled for Sept. 31 with 2-week lead time; note on the CAS sheet to turn in a single line item requisition by Sept. 16 (as printed in the manual)
entries.use: Link resources to the schedule and document actual execution statistics
entries.how: A CAS sheet becomes active when used to develop the next two-week schedule. It supports resource management (labor, tools, equipment, material, support-plan actions) and officially documents actuals in the project package. Highlight required actions and annotate whether each is a requisition or an equipment request. When an activity is complete, update actual start/finish, actual duration and actual MDs from the logbook and SITREP input (direct labor hours under the activity, excluding X-code hours). Close out the CAS sheet when updated, signed and dated by the QC inspector and project supervisor; draw a diagonal line corner to corner on the front

entries.n: Annotating the Level III Gantt Chart With Actual Progress
entries.desc: In the example, 031000 is 80% complete and 1 day ahead; 312000 (critical path) is 1 day behind and requires immediate corrective action or the project may not finish on time
entries.use: Show daily actual progress and spot activities falling behind
entries.how: Print Level III by ES date for a period and post on the jobsite information board. Daily, annotate actual progress from the logbook and CAS sheets: color the center piston black to show start, progress and finish (outside the baseline box if early/late; critical path colored red then shaded black). Solid vertical line = end of SITREP period (two-week intervals due on the 15th and last day of the month, adjust per SOP); vertical string line moves daily to current date; dashed vertical line = interim status snapshot. The vertical line deflects per activity: arrow left = behind schedule, arrow right = ahead; write percent complete after each bar (match SITREP data)
entries.dim: SITREP periods: two-week intervals, due the 15th and last day of the month

entries.desc: Uses: plan, communicate (up, down, across), and accomplish (set priorities, unity of effort). Related request forms: engineering services, excavation, road closure, utility interruption, concrete placement clearance, asphalt placement clearance
entries.use: Manage near and far horizon coordination of resources and support actions
entries.how: Built from CAS sheets, Level III Gantt, BOM and 30/60/90-day requests. Covers 14 days, revised weekly, submitted to the project manager (who presents it at the weekly operations meeting and distributes material, equipment and support requests). Part 1: work for 14 days - clear and measurable, on the Level III for that period, and shows if behind, why, and how to recover. Part 2: tool and equipment requirements. Part 3: material requirements. Near horizon (next 2 weeks): coordinate support element and subcontractor work; turn in single line item requisitions and schedule deliveries; request/confirm equipment; submit QC tests, excavation permits and support requests; act on FARs and DCDs. Far horizon (3 weeks to 3 months): follow up 30/60/90-day material and long lead items; plan subcontractor coordination; track funding; plan equipment and tool rentals. Supervisor or assistant is always on the jobsite supervising WIP
entries.dim: 14-day period; revised weekly; near horizon = next 2 weeks; far horizon = 3 weeks to 3 months
entries.wn: A deviation of even a day or two can have far-reaching impacts (concrete supplier availability, hired crane operator, added costs, support element actions)

entries.n: Support Action Request Forms (Engineering, Excavation, Road Closure, Utility Interruption)
entries.use: Request services and permits from engineering and PW/BOS in time
entries.how: Engineering Service Request: surveying, drafting, reproduction, other; date needed; description with sketch, location, size, project number. Excavation Request to PW/BOS: describe excavation and method, planned start and completion (including backfill, compaction, ground cover, paving repair), project and purpose, POC; a sketch of the planned excavation location is mandatory; routed through line crew, water crew, engineering. Road Closure Request: closure/partial closure, planned closure and reopening date/time. Utility Disruption Request: electric, water, steam, sewerage, communication, other; location; planned start and completion date/time
entries.dim: Excavation sketch is mandatory

entries.desc: Photographs of forms, reinforcing steel, anchor bolts, etc. are to be taken prior to placement of concrete
entries.use: Verify everything is ready before concrete is placed
entries.how: Part I: project, date/time desired, quantity, strength (psi), slump (in.), max aggregate size, admixtures, type of placement (roof, slab, wall, other), finish and tolerance (+/- 1/4 inch or other). Part II checklist, checked by crew leader and QC against spec: subgrade prep (elevation, dimension, compaction, capillary barrier, vapor barrier, misc.); forms (elevation, dimensions, alignment, bracing, condition, keyways, water stop, embedded items, anchor bolts, sleeves); reinforcing (size, location and spacing, chairs, bracing); electrical (conduit installed/stubbed up, sleeves, pull cords); mechanical (sleeves, subslab piping pressure tested, floor drains and cleanouts elevation/location, stubups); placing/finishing equipment (screed boards set and checked, placing and finishing tools set and checked, curing materials, testing materials such as cylinders and slump cone on site). Project supervisor submits; QC specialist approves
entries.dim: Tolerance example: +/- 1/4 inch
entries.wn: Take photographs of forms, reinforcing steel, and anchor bolts before concrete is placed

entries.use: Verify everything is ready before asphalt is placed
entries.how: Checklist parts: I subgrade prep (materials per specs, compaction, misc.); II base course (materials, compaction, embedded structures, blue top elevation); III asphalt prime (type, rate of application, application temperature, cure, edge preparation); IV asphalt mix requirements (design, extraction tests, Marshall stability, placement temperature); V equipment onsite/good condition (spreader, breakdown roller, intermediate roller, finish roller, hand tools, cleanup equipment, barricades/traffic control); VI order (specification, quantity, date of delivery). Submitted by project supervisor, approved by QC inspector

entries.n: Financial Awareness and Project Cost Worksheet
entries.desc: Project managers handle financial management; MLO controls project funds but the project supervisor is responsible to finish within the budgeted cost. Base/station fiscal departments typically hold local purchase funding
entries.use: Keep project spending within budget
entries.how: Ask: maximum funding allowed; funding remaining; enough to finish? Track with the Project Cost Worksheet: (1) original estimate within scope; (2) funds authorized/provided; (3) actual expenditure cost (received and paid); (4) pipeline cost (received or ordered, not paid); (5) future funding requirements (needed, not ordered); (6) total material and services cost = 3 + 4 + 5; (7) funding contingency = 10% of (4 + 5); (8) estimate-at-completion = 6 + 7. Every BOM add-on/reorder raises final cost and lowers remaining funds
entries.dim: Total cost = Actual + Pipeline + Future; Contingency = 0.10 x (Pipeline + Future); Estimate at Completion = Total + Contingency

entries.use: Track material from order to jobsite and control who can requisition and receive it
entries.how: Use reports from HHQ, MLO or finance, which reference BOM line item numbers; quantities must match the BOM, otherwise investigate. Track receipts using reports with the BOM and CAS sheets. Draw material from MLO using the two-week schedule and a single line item consumption/requisition document for each item. All receipts and returns are documented with that document. Submit a memo to MLO via chain of command listing personnel authorized to requisition and receive; the supervisor must be authorized. One person cannot both requisition and receive a material item. Returns of unused material are signed in red ink only by someone with signature authorization
entries.wn: Same person may not both requisition and receive the same item

entries.n: Material Issue, Lead Times and Jobsite Storage
entries.desc: Manual example: if MLO needs a lead time of 2 weeks for a concrete request and placement is scheduled for Sept. 30, note on the CAS sheet to turn in a single line item requisition by Sept. 8 (as printed in the manual)
entries.use: Request material early enough and protect it on site
entries.how: Supervisors submit single line item requisitions with the two-week schedule through the project manager. MLO normally buys no local purchase material until requested (30/60/90-day list or requisition several weeks ahead). Lead times range from several days (yard stock) to several weeks (rented equipment). Single line item requisitions can be pre-filled and kept in the package. Store materials indoors if possible or off the ground; lock up easily pilfered high-value items. Questions to answer: access for delivery, quantity needed on site, storage area size, lay-down site approved by PW/BOS, safe and secure storage, security informed, weather exposure, MSDS available. A material custodian (one per trade on large projects) handles requisition, receipt, storage, issue, inventory, return of excess, and records receipt/use in the logbook, CAS sheet and BOM, plus a damaged-materials record
entries.dim: Minimum recommended lead time for yard material from MLO: 3 days
entries.tm: Minimum 3 days for yard material; several weeks for private rental equipment

entries.use: Move identical material between projects when necessary
entries.how: A supervisor may borrow identical on-site material from another job if MLO can replace it before it is needed there; the operations officer authorizes it. Submit a Material Borrow/Transfer Request (via QC, Planning and Estimating, Operations Officer; MLO documents payback by order or reorder) and log in the Borrow/Transfer Log (borrow BOM line, loaner BOM line, date loaned, date repaid). Materials on hand may also be transferred to another project having identical materials currently requisitioned
entries.wn: Borrowing material is not recommended and must be carefully considered even for high-priority projects

entries.use: Use or return surplus material correctly
entries.how: Screen the excess list regularly published by MLO; if usable, submit a borrow/transfer request through the chain of command and cancel the original BOM purchase order by memo to MLO. Return unused issued material, specialty project tools and client-owned equipment to MLO with a single line item consumption/requisition document written in red ink; these remain project materials until transferred to the client or the client cedes ownership in writing. Submit a BOM add-on request when additional quantities of items already on the BOM are needed, or a reorder request if a new item not on the BOM is needed

entries.n: Concrete, Asphalt, Sand, or Aggregate Request
entries.use: Schedule delivery of concrete, asphalt and concrete components
entries.how: Fill out the Concrete, Asphalt, Sand, or Aggregate Request (material, date/time/amount required, sequence of delivery, specs, project and activity number); submit one copy with a single line item requisition for each BOM line item to MLO via QC. QC completes the asphalt or concrete clearance form before MLO orders; QC and MLO coordinate the final delivery schedule. Allow a minimum of 15 working days for routine scheduling. Cancelling a scheduled delivery needs 24-hour minimum notice to MLO; vendor reschedules on space/time availability, otherwise routine scheduling applies
entries.dim: Minimum 15 working days routine scheduling; cancellation notice minimum 24 hours

entries.use: Keep outstanding long lead items from stopping work
entries.how: Supervisor periodically reviews, updates and submits the project's LL items list to MLO, showing which outstanding LL items still need status monitoring. Far-horizon section of the two-week schedule tracks LL items

entries.use: Manage HM and HW safely on the jobsite
entries.how: Supervisor designates and trains a crew member as HM/HW representative per unit SOP. Together they ensure: HM inventory for the site submitted; MSDS logbook kept on site; personnel trained and follow MSDS safety measures; temporary containers labeled; spill kits at satellite HM storage areas; HM stored with compatible materials; hazardous waste handled per SOP. Inspect HM at MLO before receipt; MLO provides an MSDS and checks the item is on the unit's authorized user list. HM returned to MLO must be in original containers, serviceable condition, with the MSDS
entries.dim: No more than 2 weeks of material stored at the project site
entries.wn: No more than 2 weeks of HM may be stored at the project site

entries.desc: Tools bought with project funds are property of the client and must be offered to the client at project end
entries.use: Account for, maintain and secure project tools
entries.how: Submit signature authorization cards per unit SOP to the central tool room. Supervisor may assign a tool custodian: inventory all project tools (usually biweekly), maintain tools and resolve discrepancies, provide secure storage, set accountability (authorize tool kit custody to crew members, usually the senior in a trade; check tools in and out daily), and record lost/damaged tools for replacement (submit paperwork quickly, usually every 2 weeks at tool kit inventories). Lost tools are charged to the individual who last had custody
entries.dim: Inventory usually biweekly; daily check-in/out
entries.wn: Lost tools are charged to the individual who last had custody

entries.desc: Example from the manual: a $45,000 project completed ahead of schedule and under budget is no success if $35,800 of equipment repair and replacement results from negligence
entries.use: Take ownership of equipment, the costliest and most dangerous resource
entries.how: Consider: jobsite access, visitor parking, equipment staging, traffic flow, POL environmental protection; preventive maintenance schedule and its effect on construction schedule (coordinate with field maintenance crews instead of returning equipment to the shop; give rental equipment the same oversight); licensed and trained operators; operator accountable to the project supervisor if equipment comes with an operator; determine if equipment stays for an extended period; who checks out/turns in daily trip tickets; assign someone accountable for each piece; physical security and weekly inventory; accountability of equipment, vehicle and fuel keys and documents, including after hours. Operators use equipment for intended purpose, report abuse/neglect, and document (with photographs) any damage immediately; perform daily prestart inspections and first echelon maintenance (engine oil and coolant checks, washing, lubricating) and promptly report discrepancies. An equipment custodian may be assigned
entries.dim: Weekly equipment inventory; daily prestart

entries.use: Present the project professionally to official and unofficial visitors
entries.how: Keep the site in order, brief the crew for scheduled visits, and have visitor safety items (hard hats, ear plugs, eye protection) on hand. Meet and greet on arrival, introduce leaders, project title/number and crew; guide visitors, no one walks unescorted (except QC or safety inspectors on daily inspections); crew members find a safe breaking point before addressing visitors; get back to visitors with answers you do not know. Notify the client, PW/BOS and contracting office before visits by non-unit personnel E-8 and above. Briefing in the field office: project scope (activities, time in MDs, manpower, material, equipment), client and expectations, budget, civilian subcontractors, project management (top three QC and safety concerns, safety posture and safety rep, major hazards such as trenching, scaffolding, electrical, confined spaces, concerns, delay factors/RFIs), and progress photos
entries.dim: Notify team before visits by non-unit personnel E-8 and above
entries.eq: Hard hats, ear plugs, eye protection for visitors
entries.wn: Do not blame problems on 'they'; do not place blame on another unit. Render courtesies but never at the expense of safely stopping the work

entries.desc: Delays affect the client's plans and may affect the follow-on engineering unit schedule
entries.use: Compare scheduled to actual progress and report it to HHQ
entries.how: Monitoring uses: situation reports (SITREPs) required by supported HHQ (format per unit SOP); labor reporting and timecards; data computations for SITREP input; controlling procedures and corrective actions. HHQ conducts an in-process review at or about the 30-day mark when the operations officer and project managers set a firm schedule committing the unit to the scheduled completion date. Supervisor informs the project manager as soon as the scheduled completion date is no longer achievable; if company leadership cannot regain the schedule they inform the operations officer
entries.dim: In-process review at about 30 days

entries.use: Document construction milestones for HHQ
entries.how: Provide digital pictures of each active project on a regular basis, coordinated with SITREP comments. Use the same point of reference and broadest view over time to show sequence of progress. Also take pictures of working crews and major evolutions for historical/public affairs purposes
entries.wn: Supervisor ensures photos reflect professionalism and do not show safety violations

entries.desc: Labor accounting data feeds construction management and statistics. See appendix F
entries.use: Report labor hours in standardized categories
entries.how: Timecards use three categories: direct labor (construction activity numbers), indirect labor (codes below), and readiness and training. Indirect labor codes: XO1 Equipment, Repair, and Records; XO2 Project and Camp Maintenance Support; XO3 Project Management; XO4 Location Moving; XO5 Project Travel; XO6 Material Support; XO7 Tools; XO8 Administration and Personnel; XO9 Lost Time; XO10 Other
entries.dim: 10 indirect labor codes (XO1-XO10)

entries.desc: Labor is recorded to the nearest whole man-hour. If more than one labor category applies to a man-hour, use the dominant category
entries.use: Record actual man-hours daily and roll them into SITREP feeder data
entries.how: Prepare daily timecards of actual man-hours by all personnel assigned (rows = crew members; columns = direct labor by construction activity number, indirect codes, training; totals). Support element crew leader uses the same timecard marked support element, completes it in duplicate, and both the project supervisor and support crew leader sign; supervisor keeps a copy and turns it in with the lead element card. Record all timecard data daily on a two-week labor summary before submitting timecards through the chain of command; it feeds SITREP feeders, actual MDs per activity, and crew availability
entries.dim: Nearest whole man-hour; two-week labor summary
entries.wn: Fill out timecards honestly and accurately; timecards are the most accurate record of actual man-hours

entries.desc: Example: MA 03 Concrete completed activities total 60 percent; activity 031050 (Set Forms Beam and Canopy) is 50 percent complete and represents 18 percent of the MA, so it adds 9 percent: 60 + 9 = 69 percent. Example: MA 31 weighted 10 x 55 percent = 5.5. Example project overall 38.5 percent. Example: a 20-MD activity 25 percent complete has .75 x 20 = 15 MDs remaining. MDs remaining reflects work left to do, not MDs expended. MDs actual is not part of the SITREP to HHQ
entries.use: Calculate actual percent complete per master activity and for the project
entries.how: SITREP feeder columns: [a] MD estimate (tasked baseline), [b] weighted percent = a / total project MD estimate, [c] MA percent complete (WIP), [d] project percent complete = b x c, [e] earned MDs = a x c, [f] MDs remaining = a - e, [g] MDs actual (from timecards). Overall project percent complete = sum of column d. Compare actual WIP to scheduled percent complete (from the Level II Gantt) to find percent deviation. For each MA in progress complete a Master Activity Percent Complete worksheet: weighted percent = CA MD estimate / total MA MD estimate; total work and work complete (linear feet, square feet, cubic yards...); CA percent complete = work complete / total work; MA percent complete contribution = weighted percent x CA percent complete; MDs remaining = percent of work remaining x MD estimate. WIP is 0 for MAs not started and 100 for completed MAs. Add a comments line describing work since last SITREP; if actual WIP is less than scheduled WIP, explain the delay and give the recovery plan
entries.dim: d = b x c; e = a x c; f = a - e; Weighted % = a / total MD estimate; MDs remaining = (1 - % complete) x MD estimate
entries.wn: If actual WIP falls behind scheduled WIP by more than the HHQ-allowed percent deviation, the unit must advise HHQ, include a plan to get back on schedule, and request approval for any needed changes to the Level I or Level II Gantt chart

entries.n: Man-Days Earned Method for Percent Complete
entries.desc: Example: activity 031050 at 50 percent of 25 MDs = 12.5 or 13 MDs earned; MA 03: 97 / 140 = .69 = 69 percent; project 179 / 454 = .394 = 39.4 percent. Results differ slightly from the WIP method because of rounding to whole MDs
entries.use: Alternative way to calculate project percent complete
