entries.desc: Wastewater containing black water must be managed as black water, so keep gray water separate. Construct urine disposal facilities next to male latrines. Establish and enforce conservation standards such as 4-minute showers and immediate repair of leaks. Use grease traps or oil-water separators where applicable
entries.use: Reducing black-water and gray-water load
entries.how: Keep gray water separate from black water, build urine disposal next to male latrines, enforce short showers and fix leaks
entries.dim: Shower limit example: 4 minutes

entries.n: Set up recycling and reuse program
entries.desc: Initiate recycling/reuse for plastics, cardboard, paper, batteries, tires, wood, aluminum cans and other metals (ferrous and nonferrous). Requires source segregation, sorting facilities, compactors sized for the base, and enough recyclable material to justify the program. Consider composting for food waste and land farming for petroleum-contaminated soils. Establish consolidated storage yards for construction materials and common-use items. Maintenance facilities maximize reuse of petroleum products, fuels and fluids
entries.use: Reducing disposal volume on a base
entries.how: Start source segregation and consolidated reuse yard for the listed materials when base size and threat allow

entries.desc: Place trash receptacles and recycle bins together in a convenient location with signs explaining what goes in each. Use barriers (size/shape of container openings) to prevent mixing waste types. Do not make waste and recycling containers the same color; associate a color with each material. If no colored bins, paint words on the outside. Segregate as near as possible to the point of generation to conserve time/manpower/money, reduce spills and littering, and minimize exposure
entries.use: Getting soldiers to sort waste correctly
entries.how: Put trash and recycle bins together, label them in words readable even in the dark, and use opening shapes to prevent mixing

entries.desc: DLA Disposition Services (formerly DRMO) handles disposition of excess property, HW, and property requiring demilitarization; reuse/recycling programs including electronics; HAZMAT assistance; helps complete documents, arrange disposal contracts, and train personnel in turn-in procedures. DLA can dispose of items in place (large items, remote property, property it cannot accept). If DLA cannot take physical custody it provides procedures for management and disposal
entries.use: Excess property, hazardous waste, demilitarization items
entries.how: Contact DLA Disposition Services for turn-in paperwork, disposal contracts, training, and in-place disposal of items that cannot be moved

entries.desc: Environmental officer (commissioned or NCO) designated in writing by the commander, trained per AR 200-1 (USMC: MCO P5090.2A, battalion/squadron and above). Manages environmental issues and records, includes waste systems in inspections, ensures adequate PPE, spill response supplies, HWAP materials and waste packaging/marking supplies, reviews contracts for waste minimization/green procurement, develops waste-handling SOP, and conducts periodic assessments
entries.use: Company/battalion environmental program
entries.how: Army commanders appoint an environmental officer (Marine Corps: environmental compliance coordinator) in writing and train them
entries.eq: PPE, spill response supplies, HWAP materials, packaging/marking supplies

entries.desc: Members: engineers, logisticians, PVNTMED, safety officer, Civil Affairs, CBRN, environmental officer, CORs, transporters. Facilitator synchronizes efforts, recommends priorities, manages information, monitors waste streams continuously, disseminates policy to first-line leaders. Convene regularly; brief commander and staff regularly
entries.use: Staff coordination of waste issues
entries.how: Commander can form a working group with a facilitator to synchronize waste efforts and brief the commander regularly

entries.n: Maintain accountability and documentation of waste sites
entries.desc: Document conditions including preexisting conditions, changes during deployment and conditions at closure using digital photos/videos, maps and required environmental documentation. Write contracts so contractor is liable for environmental impacts, with CORs/escorts to ensure compliance. Include waste management in command inspections. Record waste management in SOPs including spill prevention and response
entries.use: Limiting liability and supporting closure
entries.how: Photograph and document conditions before, during and at closure; write contractor liability into contracts

entries.desc: During transitions the base camp population can double for a couple of weeks, increasing waste. Transients and HN contractor employees also vary population. Monitor system status to anticipate when design capacities will be exceeded; plan equipment, funding and space from base camp inception
entries.use: Base camp transitions, right-seat rides
entries.how: Design capacity with a surge margin for transfers of authority
entries.dim: Population can double for a couple of weeks during transitions

entries.desc: Step 1 Analyze the situation (mission variables, RFIs, recon); Step 2 Develop preliminary waste estimates (one level down, look two levels down; combat planning factors in lb/day solid, gal/day liquid); Step 3 Categorize waste requirements; Step 4 Evaluate waste management capabilities (manpower, equipment, materials, funding; requirements-vs-capabilities matrix); Step 5 Generate solutions (feasible, suitable, sustainable; troop-to-task analysis); Step 6 Integrate tasks into plans and orders (engineer or sustainment annex; see appendix B)
entries.use: Developing a plan for each waste stream
entries.how: Run steps 1-6 in parallel with MDMP: analyze, estimate, categorize, evaluate capabilities, generate solutions, integrate into orders
entries.wn: Do not assume LOGCAP/contractor will handle it without detailed planning objectives, timelines and management expectations

entries.desc: Immediate: less than 72 hours (main concern solid waste and black water). Basic: sustain operations a minimum of 60 days and up to six months; field-expedient methods continue, source segregation and burn pit, contracts/septic/lagoon, HWAPs. Expanded: minimum 180 days and up to two to five years; burn pits no longer allowed without proper approval; contract/landfill/incinerator, wastewater connections or treatment, HWSA. Enhanced: more than two years and up to ten years; facilities life expectancy more than 2 and less than 10 years. Transfer and closure: as directed by geographic combatant command and DLA (HW)
entries.use: Matching waste solutions to how long you will stay
entries.how: Pick the category by expected stay: Immediate, Basic, Expanded, Enhanced, Transfer/Closure
entries.dim: Immediate <72 hr; Basic min 60 days to 6 months; Expanded min 180 days to 2-5 years; Enhanced >2 years to 10 years

entries.n: Waste treatment/disposal options by duration (Table 2-4 summary)
entries.desc: See table TM56-T2-4 for the full matrix. Notes: existing infrastructure considered first (may need HN approval); containerizing is temporary; some construction (septic, lagoons) needs technical expertise; a grease trap or oil-water separator is required for POL-contaminated water
entries.use: Picking a method for a given waste stream and time horizon
entries.how: Use Table 2-4 for first-cut options; always consider existing infrastructure first

entries.n: Site separation rules (what not to put near what)
entries.desc: Do not locate billeting or drainage features near HAZMAT/HW storage areas or motor pools. Do not construct dining facilities, food storage or water distribution near latrines or wastewater disposal. Do not plan landfills, incinerators or burn pits upwind of the base camp or billeting. Do not construct billeting in low-lying flood-prone areas or near confined domestic animals. Do not excavate inside the perimeter (drainage impacts). Do not locate waste sites in areas easily scavenged by the HN population. Collocate compatible areas to share fencing, berms, roads, offices, recordkeeping
entries.use: Layout of base camp waste-related areas
entries.how: Keep dining/water away from latrines and waste water; keep billeting away from HW and motor pools; keep burn/landfill sites downwind

entries.n: Weather and terrain effects on waste systems
entries.desc: Warm temperatures and low humidity improve absorption/evaporation in lagoons and combustion rates. High humidity and cloud cover hinder evaporation. Extreme cold impedes digging, freezes wastewater piping, slows absorption/evaporation. Optimal compost decay temperature range 70 F to 100 F. Rain and snowmelt can render low areas unusable and overflow containment. Position waste systems downwind and down gradient. Plan around soil type, drainage, water table depth, slope, flood plains, wetlands
entries.use: Checking whether a site/method works in current conditions
entries.how: Warm/dry helps evaporation and burning; cold, humid, cloudy hinders; compost needs warmth
entries.dim: Compost optimal temperature: 70 F to 100 F

entries.desc: Table 2-3 sample: Battalion (700 personnel) immediate nonhazardous solid waste 2,800 pounds/day and wastewater 1,400 gallons/day. Where quantities cannot be determined (HW, special, medical), annotate the primary sources (activity/task). Basis: task organization, unit functions (maintenance, medical, food services), equipment densities, basic loads/stockage lists, HAZMAT inventories and SDSs, mission variables
entries.use: Quick estimate of daily waste by unit
entries.how: Build matrix per subordinate unit: solid waste lb/day, wastewater gal/day, HW/special, medical
entries.dim: Battalion of 700 personnel: 2,800 lb/day solid waste; 1,400 gal/day wastewater (sample)

entries.desc: Hazards assessed for risk (low, moderate, high, extremely high) by probability (frequent, likely, occasional, seldom, unlikely) and severity (catastrophic, critical, marginal, negligible). Present priorities of effort and support to commander. See appendix A and ATP 5-19
entries.use: Prioritizing which waste stream to solve first
entries.how: Assign probability x severity to each stream to get low/moderate/high/extremely high risk and recommend priorities

entries.n: Nonhazardous solid waste generation planning factors
entries.desc: Basic services start at 4 lb/person/day; expanded 6; enhanced 10. Estimate = rate x number of personnel x days. Characterization studies found higher rates: 18.2 lb/person/day (USACE, 14 days sorting at Balkans base camp, 2006) and 15.9 lb/person/day as reasonable planning factor (Afghanistan, 2011, plus 18.2). 1,000 pounds approximately 1 cubic yard (compaction dependent). Hub bases and senior headquarters generate more; reliance on nonlocal supplies raises packaging waste; local purchase lowers it. Worked examples: Battalion 700 persons x 4 = 2,800 lb/day x 60 days = 168,000 lb = 168 cu yd; Battalion 700 x 6 = 4,200 lb/day x 180 days = 756,000 lb = 756 cu yd; Company 100 x 4 = 400 lb/day x 60 = 24,000 lb = 24 cu yd; Company 100 x 6 = 600 lb/day x 180 = 108,000 lb = 108 cu yd
entries.use: Estimating daily and total solid waste for a unit
entries.how: Multiply persons x lb/person/day x days; use 4 (basic), 6 (expanded), 10 (enhanced) lb/person/day as starting points
entries.dim: Basic 4 lb/person/day; expanded 6; enhanced 10; studies 15.9 and 18.2 lb/person/day; 1,000 lb ~ 1 cu yd
entries.wn: Waste is produced as shipments arrive and are unpacked, not just post-consumer

entries.desc: Place waste in clear disposable plastic bags (visibility of contents), tie, consolidate at designated collection points. Break down and bind cardboard boxes. Segregate dining facility waste. Containers: closable (dumpsters or cans with lids), leakproof, noncombustible, nonabsorbent, corrosion-resistant, with lifting handles. Food waste in tight-fitting covered, nonabsorbent, leakproof, easily cleaned containers with handles; clean per TB MED 530. Appoint a collection point manager; put duties in SOP. Locate collection points conveniently, secure from scavengers. Temporary storage must not create health/fire hazard, attract insects/rodents, or cause litter
entries.use: Setting up trash collection
entries.how: Bag in clear plastic bags, tie, consolidate at collection points at least 100 ft from dining; remove food waste daily and other waste at least every two days
entries.dim: Collection points at least 100 feet from dining facilities; removal: food service facilities daily, other nonhazardous solid waste at least every two days

entries.n: Solid waste collection vehicle and transport
entries.desc: Use a dedicated collection vehicle with a low tailgate, cover to prevent blow-out, and PPE to retrieve spills. Clean before use for other missions. Vehicles later used to carry food are cleaned and disinfected with chlorine solution: 6.4 ounces of bleach per 1 gallon of water = 200 ppm. Avoid double-handling, maintain segregation, state quantities (tons/cu yd) in transport tasks, minimize routes through billeting areas, perform dust abatement
entries.use: Hauling trash safely
entries.how: Dedicate a vehicle with low tailgate and cover; clean before other use; disinfect with 200 ppm chlorine before carrying food
entries.dim: 200 ppm chlorine = 6.4 oz bleach per 1 gal water

entries.desc: Transfer stations gather waste when distance to disposal is too far for economical direct haul, movement is restricted/hazardous, local contractor access is limited to on-call, or small collection trucks are used. On base camps, locate near contractor access gates (search areas) with barriers preventing access to rest of camp
entries.use: Gathering waste when landfill is far or access restricted
entries.how: Place near contractor access gate with barriers so contractors cannot enter rest of camp

entries.desc: Site selected rapidly by officer or NCO in charge and excavated with organic resources. After waste is deposited, cap with soil and report location through chain of command. Must follow published solid waste disposal guidelines, including recording and reporting burial location
entries.use: Maneuver unit in operational pause in close combat
entries.how: OIC/NCOIC picks site, digs with available means, deposits waste, caps with soil, reports location
entries.wn: Aboveground waste piles or open dumps are not allowed

entries.desc: Pits preferred for overnight halts. Pit 4 feet square and 4 feet deep suitable for 1 day for a unit of 100 individuals. Fill to within 1 foot of top; cover with 1-foot mound of compacted dirt. For halts longer than 2 days a continuous trench is preferable
entries.use: Unit on the move or stationary less than 1 week; overnight halts
entries.how: Dig a 4 ft x 4 ft x 4 ft pit for a 100-person unit per day; fill to within 1 ft of top, then mound 1 ft of compacted dirt
entries.dim: Pit 4 ft x 4 ft x 4 ft deep; 100 persons per day; fill to within 1 ft of top; 1 ft compacted mound; location at least 100 m from natural water source used for cooking/drinking and at least 30 m from field kitchens and eating areas

entries.desc: Trench first dug about 2 feet wide, 4 feet deep, long enough to accommodate first day's garbage. Fill to within 1 foot of top and cover with 1-foot mound of compacted dirt. Extend trench as required; excavated dirt covers garbage already deposited; repeat daily
entries.use: Halts longer than 2 days (up to less than 1 week)
entries.how: Dig trench about 2 ft wide, 4 ft deep, long enough for day 1; extend daily and use spoil to cover prior waste
entries.dim: Trench about 2 ft wide x 4 ft deep; fill to within 1 ft of top; 1 ft compacted mound

entries.n: Burial site siting and closure marking
entries.desc: Burial sites at least 100 meters from any natural water source used for cooking or drinking (stream, lake, pond, well) and at least 30 meters from field kitchens and eating areas. At closure place signage indicating type of pit or trench, date closed, and unit designation if situation allows. Record an 8-digit grid coordinate for each site and report to higher headquarters
entries.use: Locating and closing burial pits/trenches
entries.how: Keep 100 m from drinking/cooking water and 30 m from kitchens; on closure, mark type, date, unit and record an 8-digit grid
entries.dim: At least 100 m from drinking/cooking water; at least 30 m from field kitchens/eating areas; 8-digit grid

entries.desc: Sanitary landfill: waste spread, compacted and covered with soil daily. Landfills at least 10,000 feet from airfields (bird strikes). Waste-to-cover ratio generally 4:1; POL-contaminated dirt may be used as cover. Not within 100-year flood plain; not high water table; need clearance between water table and lowest point. Not suitable on hilltops, highly permeable areas (gravel beds), swamps/marshes, natural drainage channels, wildlife sanctuaries/threatened species habitat, flood plains, karst, steep slopes. Avoid underground utilities. Best on flat or gently rolling terrain not subject to flooding; ravines/quarries can work with cover and runoff control. Plan leachate management and closure from initial design
entries.use: Choosing a landfill location
entries.how: Keep at least 10,000 ft from airfields; outside 100-year flood plain; downstream from water; need 4:1 waste-to-cover ratio of cover soil
entries.dim: At least 10,000 ft from airfields; waste-to-cover ratio 4:1; outside 100-year flood plain
entries.wn: Resource-intensive long-term solution; consult USACE/APHC reachback first

entries.desc: Report date opened and closed and accurate map coordinates to higher headquarters. Photograph history from preconstruction to closure. Goals: minimize future maintenance/monitoring, minimize future environmental impacts, prepare site for future use. Include closure in initial design
entries.use: Closing a landfill
entries.how: Report open/close dates and map coordinates; keep photo history from preconstruction to closure

entries.desc: Burn pit = area without commercial incinerator used to burn solid waste outdoors at a location with more than 100 attached/assigned personnel and in place longer than 90 days. Least preferred method. Use per DODI 4715.19; operational commander must approve a solid waste management plan; short-term solution with minimal disposal. Covered waste cannot be burned unless no alternative, with determinations to USD(A&S) and justification every 180 calendar days. Plan transition to incinerator/engineered landfill ASAP. Separate noncombustibles (metal) for recycling. Burn completely to ash; when not burning cover with 4 to 6 inches of soil. At closure report open/close dates and grid coordinates; closure photos for ESCR
entries.use: Last-resort solid waste burning when burial/contract not possible
entries.how: Allowed only if in approved solid waste management plan; site at least 450 ft downwind from inhabited areas; cover 4-6 in. soil when not burning
entries.dim: Burn pits at least 450 ft from and downwind of inhabited areas; applies at >100 personnel and >90 days; cover 4-6 in. soil; justification every 180 days for covered waste
entries.wn: Covered waste (never burn): HW, medical waste, tires, treated wood, batteries, plastics (except insignificant amounts), munitions/explosives, compressed gas cylinders, fuel containers, aerosol cans, PCBs, POL products (other than starter fuel), asbestos, mercury, foam tent material, any item containing these. Also avoid rubber, tar paper, asphalt shingles, drywall, paint, thinner/strippers, pesticides and containers, appliances/electrical equipment, wires. No lithium batteries or heavy metals

entries.desc: Separate dining facility waste from burn (wet waste reduces combustion); strain garbage with coarse strainer (old bucket, can, or oil drum with holes punched in bottom); incinerate solids, pour liquids through grease trap into soakage pit. Prevent low-heat/smoldering fires with ample ventilation and measured fuel. Burn only under meteorological conditions that protect downwind populations and promote plume lofting. Do not burn in flight paths or near HAZMAT/fuel storage. Fence or berm and limit access, daily cover vs vectors. Trained operators inspect contents of each tipping vehicle or bag for prohibited items; fixed operating hours (usually daylight); alert base camp fire service before daily burning. Maintain fuel, fire extinguishers, communications, hand tools, PPE on site. Emergency response team and procedures
entries.use: Operating any burn pit or incinerator safely
entries.how: Burn only dry waste, with ample ventilation, at the right times, with trained operators, PPE, fire service alert and fencing
entries.dim: Burn pits at least 450 ft from inhabited areas
entries.eq: PPE (respiratory, biohazard, heat, fire), fire extinguishers, grease trap
entries.wn: Burn barrels/open burning only in emergencies until incinerators obtained

entries.desc: Driven by need to dispose of accumulated waste for operational security/combat effectiveness/agility and hasty burial not viable. Natural depression or rapidly excavated depression used as burn pit; fuel source applied and ignited; after contents eliminated cap with soil; report location through chain of command. Follow published disposal guidelines
entries.use: Maneuver unit when hasty burial not viable
entries.how: OIC/NCOIC picks natural or quick-dug depression, adds fuel, ignites, caps with soil after burn, reports location

entries.desc: Stack from 55-gallon drum with both ends cut out, or one end cut out and other end punched with holes for draft. Holes punched through sides and steel rods inserted to form a grate. Set drum on rocks, bricks or other nonflammable material. Build fire under drum; add waste one shovelful at a time on top of grate. Handles solid waste of a company-size or smaller unit. Wet material disrupts draft
entries.use: Company-size or smaller unit dry trash
entries.how: Make from a 55-gallon drum with grate of steel rods; add waste one shovelful at a time
entries.dim: 55-gallon drum; steel rods for grate
entries.wn: Open burning; permitted only if theater guidance allows

entries.desc: Insert a sheet of metal through telescoped oil drums with both ends removed. Metal plane extends approximately 2 feet beyond upper end of drums as loading/stoking platform. Grate at lower end of plane; wood or fuel-oil fire built under grate. When hot, place drained garbage on stoking platform; as it dries push down incline in small amounts; final combustion on grate. Minimally affected by wind/rain; takes time and skill to build
entries.use: Battalion-size unit solid waste
entries.how: Telescoped oil drums with metal plane and grate; push drained garbage down incline in small amounts
entries.dim: Plane extends ~2 ft beyond upper end of barrels
entries.wn: Open burning; permitted only if theater guidance allows

entries.n: Burn barrel / inclined-plane burner operating rules
entries.desc: Operate from 3 hours after sunrise to 3 hours before sunset for smoke dispersion. Use approximately 1 gallon of fuel per cubic meter of waste. Locate downwind of work and billeting areas. Trained operators, PPE and fire extinguishers on hand; keep area around burners free of refuse; manage delivery so not overloaded; allow time for cleaning and trimming fire before closing. Allow 0.5 to 0.75 man-hours per ton of refuse processed (excluding residue removal and major repairs)
entries.use: Running field burners
entries.how: Operate 3 hr after sunrise to 3 hr before sunset, ~1 gal fuel per cubic meter, 0.5-0.75 man-hours per ton
entries.dim: ~1 gal fuel per cubic meter waste; 0.5 to 0.75 man-hours per ton; hours 3 hr after sunrise to 3 hr before sunset

entries.desc: Incinerators have enclosed combustion chambers, reduce waste volume and pollution. Place on concrete pads built to carry the incinerator and vehicles. Nonhazardous solid waste incinerators will not be used for HW or medical waste (these need specific incinerators). Needs trained operators, manufacturer training, feeding system, controlled air/temperature/fuel/time; calibrate and record maintenance. Ash and noncombustibles: transport for disposal, characterize (PVNTMED help); ash with hazardous constituents disposed as HW, otherwise nonhazardous solid waste, generally buried. Smoke/flame signature may prevent use for operational security
entries.use: Enclosed controlled burning at base camps
entries.how: Put on concrete pad; train operators; test ash; ash with hazardous constituents is HW, else bury

entries.desc: Air curtain introduces controlled velocity air across upper combustion chamber trapping unburned particles in high-temperature zone where temperatures can reach 1,800 F. Burn boxes designed for wood waste only; no dual combustion chamber or stack; not designed for solid waste (food waste or plastic)
entries.use: Wood waste only
entries.how: Use only for wood; air curtain traps particles at up to 1,800 F
entries.dim: Up to 1,800 F
entries.wn: Wet waste or plastic may exceed long-term exposure guidelines for coarse particles

entries.desc: Compostable: sewage sludge, uncontaminated food waste (no grease/oil), wood debris, cardboard, paper. Base camp population of 2,500 generates approximately 5,500 cubic meters or 1,500 tons of compostable waste (including sludge) per year. Site: concrete slab with drainage and overhead cover, pole barn, or engineered site (6 inches compacted well-graded gravel over 12 inches compacted engineered base over compacted low-permeable native soil or impermeable geotextile; do percolation tests if permeability unknown). Maximum site slope 3 percent. Runoff to retention pond (may need liner; treat if petroleum sheen). All-weather roads, possibly power. Steps: item screening, ingredient preparation, active composting, curing, application. Screen out HAZMAT and noncompostables. Compost uses: soil amendment, landfill cover, erosion control, dust abatement, bulking in land farming, bioremediation
entries.use: Reducing organic waste volume
entries.how: Compare compost vs burn/bury; a 2,500-person camp makes ~1,500 tons (5,500 cu m) compostable per year; site max 3 percent slope
entries.dim: 2,500 persons ~ 5,500 cu m or 1,500 tons/yr; gravel 6 in. over 12 in. engineered base; max slope 3 percent

entries.desc: Aerated static pile: pumped air and semipermeable membrane cover, 6 to 9 weeks, needs PVC aeration pipes, blowers, probes, computer, membrane cover, chipper or tub grinder, star/trommel screen, 2.5-5 cu yd bucket loader; area ~5,000 sq m per 1,500 annual tons or 5,500 annual cu m. Windrow: rows ~1 meter high, turned or passively aerated, finished compost 3 months to 2 years; needs tractor with turner, thermometers and oxygen probes, water tank, heavy-duty chipper (tub grinder not recommended), manure spreader, screen, loader; area ~15,000 sq m per 1,500 tons/yr; may be least effective for base camp. In-vessel: enclosed aerated vessel plus 3-8 weeks curing in windrows, total ~11 weeks; camp producing 5 cu m compostable/day uses ~5 cu m bulking agent/day, so a 3-week cycle needs six 40-cubic-meter containers; area ~5,000 sq m
entries.use: Choosing aerated static pile, windrow or in-vessel
entries.how: Static pile: 6-9 weeks, ~5,000 sq m per 1,500 tons/yr; windrow: 3 months-2 years, ~15,000 sq m; in-vessel ~11 weeks
entries.dim: Windrow height ~1 m; static pile 6-9 weeks; windrow 3 months-2 yr; in-vessel ~11 weeks; 6 x 40 cu m containers for 5 cu m/day, 3-week cycle
entries.eq: Chipper, screen, 2.5-5 cu yd loader, blowers/probes (static/in-vessel), tractor/windrow turner (windrow)

entries.n: Land farming area for petroleum-contaminated soil
entries.desc: Land farming area needs impermeable surface (concrete or landfill liner) and controls so contaminated dirt does not leach to groundwater. Compost and sludge can be used as micronutrients in bioremediation. Same equipment used for composting can be used
entries.use: Bioremediation of POL-contaminated soil
entries.how: Use an impermeable surface (concrete or landfill liner) with controls; same equipment as composting

entries.desc: MWR: aluminum cans, plastic bottles, cardboard, plastic food containers. Kitchens: cans, bottles, plastic containers, cardboard, steel cans, pallets, food waste (livestock feed where allowed). Supply: cardboard, packing materials, pallets. Maintenance: aluminum cans, plastic bottles, cardboard, scrap metal, used oil and antifreeze, wood pallets, recoverable parts. Construction: debris, packing materials. Ensure recyclables are not contaminated with hazardous substances, need not go to DLA, or need demilitarization; remove all U.S. identification markings by painting or sanding before turnover to non-U.S. entities. Mixing with food waste generally renders recyclables nonrecyclable
entries.use: Knowing what each area generates
entries.how: MWR, kitchens, supply, maintenance and construction produce specific recyclables; remove U.S. markings before handing to non-U.S. entities

entries.n: Solid waste management facility layout best practices
entries.desc: Drop-off open circulation area sized for typical vehicles with multiple bins (metals, plastics, wood). Administration building with view of operations, scales near it, maintenance building central, access for large trucks away from main traffic. Sorting area with concrete floor and pole barn, near compactor and burn/incineration area; consider belt picking system for large bases. Ash pit adjacent to burn/incineration area. Compacting area near sorting and drop-off, metal preengineered building for balers/compactors. Composting area close to sorting and ash pit. Optional power generation near highest loads, concrete pads with secondary containment under generators; buried power lines preferred
entries.use: Designing a base solid waste yard
entries.how: Co-locate drop-off, sorting, compacting, composting, ash pit and admin with supervisor view and scales near admin

entries.desc: Departing unit responsible for proper environmental closure/transfer. Closure plan addresses reusable/recyclable materials, termination of contracts, deconstruction waste, closure/cleanup of incinerators, burn pits, ash pits, composting and land farming sites, HAZMAT/HW and HWAP cleanup, equipment cleaning, medical waste, latrine closure/marking, wastewater lagoons and treatment, storage tanks, sorting/compacting/drop-off areas, trash receptacles, generators/fuel bladders/secondary containment liners, berms, landfill closure and marking. Permanent closure of open-burning site: inform tenant commanders, secure access, fill in burn pit depressions, transfer historical records. Record grid coordinates and take post-closure photos/videos for the ESCR (EBS + ECRs + ESCS are basis)
entries.use: Base camp transfer/closure
entries.how: Close burn pits, ash pits, landfills, compost/land farm sites, and record grid coordinates and photos for the ESCR

entries.desc: Gray water: laundry, showers, hand-washing devices, washracks, water purification systems; dining facility wastewater can be gray if unlikely to contain pathogens. Black water: toilet wastewater and kitchen wastewater containing food wastes (food prep areas, dishwashers, garbage disposals); includes waste from service animals such as military working dogs. Wastewater containing black water is managed as black water. Discharge of untreated wastewater to streams/rivers/water bodies is prohibited; a 'pump and dump' strategy is unacceptable. Do not assume contractors will be available immediately
entries.use: Deciding how to manage a wastewater stream
entries.how: Black water = may contain pathogens (toilets, food-waste kitchen water); gray = laundry, showers, hand-washing, washracks, water purification
entries.wn: Never discharge untreated wastewater to water bodies

entries.desc: Drum or box divided vertically into unequal chambers by a wooden baffle extending to within 1 inch of the bottom. Waste poured through strainer into large chamber, passes under baffle to small chamber. Large chamber has removable lid and strainer (box with openings in bottom filled with straw or burlap); scrub strainer with soap and water. 1-inch pipe inserted 3 to 6 inches below top of smaller chamber carries liquid to soakage pit. Clean frequently: remove grease, drain trap, remove sediment. Trap must be large enough that hot greasy water does not heat water already in trap, else grease passes through. Contents burned or landfilled per theater guidance
entries.use: Dining facility/kitchen wastewater before soakage pit
entries.how: Build from a 55-gallon drum or box with wooden baffle to within 1 in. of the bottom; strain through straw/burlap; discharge pipe to soakage pit
entries.dim: 55-gallon drum; baffle to within 1 in. of bottom; 1 in. outlet pipe 3-6 in. below top of small chamber
entries.eq: 55-gallon drum or box, wooden baffle, strainer, straw/burlap, 1-in. pipe

entries.desc: Barrel (30 to 55 gallon) with top removed and large holes bored in bottom; 8 inches gravel or small stones in bottom, covered with 12 to 18 inches of clean wood ashes or sand; burlap fastened at top as coarse strainer. Place directly over soakage pit (remove bottom instead of boring holes) or on platform with trough to pit. Empty every 2 days: wash trap, dispose of ashes/sand, refill with fresh. Wash burlap daily or replace
entries.use: Field kitchen wastewater over a soakage pit
entries.how: Take 30-55 gal barrel, bore holes in bottom, 8 in. gravel then 12-18 in. ashes or sand, burlap on top; empty every 2 days
entries.dim: 30-55 gal barrel; 8 in. gravel; 12-18 in. ashes or sand; empty every 2 days
entries.tm: Empty trap every 2 days; wash burlap daily

entries.n: Oil-water separator for motor pools and washracks
entries.desc: Used for runoff from motor pools, POL storage areas, washrack activities. Areas built with impermeable surfaces; coordinate location with environmental officer before construction. Prevent dumping of POL, solvents, antifreeze into drainage. It is a filtering mechanism, not a disposal system. Do not use emulsifying agents (soaps, detergents, solvents). Keep trash cans nearby. Inspect regularly. Routinely remove surface oil (e.g., suction to approved tank truck). Oil and oily sludge may go to reuse/recovery, incineration, DLA Disposition Services, waste hauler, landfill, land farming; sludge may be HW if pollutants exceed limits
entries.use: POL-contaminated runoff from motor pools, POL storage, washracks
entries.how: Build impermeable surfaces, coordinate with environmental officer, ban emulsifiers, skim oil routinely
entries.wn: POL-contaminated water requires a grease trap or oil-water separator

entries.desc: Collocate urine disposal facilities with male latrines. At least one urine disposal facility for each male latrine or for every 100 male personnel. Commercial off-the-shelf urine collection devices usable on the move. Urine alone handled in urine facilities reduces latrine area/resources
entries.use: Male latrine support
entries.how: Provide at least one urine disposal facility per male latrine or per 100 male personnel
entries.dim: 1 per male latrine or per 100 male personnel

entries.n: Urine soakage pit with pipe urinals
entries.desc: Pit 4 feet square and 4 feet deep filled with aggregate (rocks, brick, broken glass, nonporous rubble); covered with small stones forming 4-inch-deep surface layer extending 6 inches past pit edge on all sides. Use pipe urinals with funnels or trough urinals; no urination onto pit surface. Optional ventilating shafts with screened openings from about 8 inches above pit to within 6 inches of bottom. Clean funnels/troughs daily with soap and water. Pipe urinals: at least 1 inch diameter, approximately 38 inches long, at each corner (and halfway along sides if needed), inserted at least 8 inches below pit surface; tar paper or sheet metal funnel with screen, upper rim about 30 inches above ground. Use soakage trench instead if groundwater or bedrock prevents digging pit
entries.use: Field urine disposal
entries.how: Dig 4 ft x 4 ft x 4 ft pit, fill with rock/rubble, 4 in. stone layer extending 6 in. past pit edges; pipe urinals 1 in. x 38 in
entries.dim: Pit 4 ft x 4 ft x 4 ft deep; 4 in. stone layer, 6 in. overlap; pipes >=1 in. dia x ~38 in. long, >=8 in. below surface, funnel rim ~30 in. above ground
entries.eq: Rock/brick/rubble, pipes, funnels, screen, soap and water
entries.wn: Never pour oil or grease into the pit

entries.desc: Trough U- or V-shaped, approximately 10 feet long, of sheet metal or wood (wood lined with heavy tar paper). Legs cut slightly shorter on one end so trough slopes down to a pipe carrying urine to a soakage pit
entries.use: More durable urine facility where materials available
entries.how: 10 ft U- or V-shaped trough of sheet metal or tar-paper-lined wood, sloped to a pipe to soakage pit
entries.dim: Trough about 10 ft long
entries.eq: Sheet metal or wood, tar paper, pipe

entries.desc: Acceptable only where groundwater level is more than 3 feet below the surface. 55-gallon drum containing oil placed over a recessed soakage pit; waste POL can be used, vegetable oil preferred. Urine enters through screen and sinks through oil; urine rises in a 3-inch-diameter vertically braced pipe until reaching an overflow pipe in center of drum that sends it to soakage pit. Screen lifted with hooks for debris removal. Operates as long as soakage pit accepts urine
entries.use: Urine disposal where groundwater is more than 3 ft below surface
entries.how: 55-gallon drum containing oil (vegetable oil preferred) over a recessed soakage pit; oil seals against odor and flies
entries.dim: Groundwater >3 ft below surface; 55-gal drum; 3 in. diameter pipe

entries.desc: When abandoned or clogged: spray with approved residual insecticide, cover with a 1-foot mound of compacted dirt, place rectangular sign on mound indicating type of pit and date closed
entries.use: Abandoning or clogged urine pit
entries.how: Spray with approved residual insecticide, cover with 1-ft compacted mound, post sign with type and date
entries.dim: 1 ft compacted mound

entries.desc: Field methods: evaporation beds, soakage pits, soakage trenches (typical when on the move, short stays, initial base camp). Constructed for small volumes. Kitchen and washrack water needs grease trap/oil-water separator first. Not suitable in cold environments or high water tables; alternatives are constructed wetlands, holding basins, or containing gray water in tanks/drums for removal. Use percolation tests and technical guidance; earthmoving equipment may be needed. Prefer existing treatment facilities, purple pipe reuse
entries.use: Short-duration or early-stage gray water disposal
entries.how: Use evaporation beds, soakage pits or soakage trenches; pretreat kitchen and washrack water with grease trap/OWS first

entries.desc: Locate outside base camp in open, sunny area. Scrape topsoil to edges forming small dike. Spade ground 10 to 15 inches deep; rake into rows with ridges approximately 6 inches above depression (lengthwise or crosswise for best distribution). Build so waste can go to any one of the beds. Rotation: flood one bed per day to top of ridges (average depth 3 inches); allow to evaporate and percolate; after 3 or 4 days respade and reform. Flood other beds on successive days. Three-tier beds usable when land is limited. Get technical support for percolation test, daily effluent, application rate and acreage
entries.use: Larger gray water volumes in hot, dry climates, high water table or clay soil
entries.how: Spade 10-15 in. deep, rake rows with ridges ~6 in. high, flood one bed per day to ~3 in. average depth, rest 3-4 days
entries.dim: Spade depth 10-15 in.; ridges ~6 in.; flood to ~3 in. average depth; rest 3-4 days

entries.desc: Soakage pit 4 to 6 feet deep, square or rectangular; size from percolation test and estimated effluent. If occupied several weeks, build pits in pairs and alternate daily. Pits no deeper than 6 feet (avoid shoring). Bottom at least 2 feet above groundwater table and 5 feet above rock/impermeable soil. Located outside base camp and at least 100 feet down gradient from any water source. For more flow, make longer rectangular pit (not deeper) or several pits with equal distribution; distance between pits at least twice the size of the pits. Absorption area is the sidewall area, not the bottom. Closure: backfill and compact with soil 1 foot above grade, mark with rectangular sign (contents, date closed, unit), document 8-digit grid
entries.use: Gray water disposal where soil percolates
entries.how: 4-6 ft deep square/rectangle, no deeper than 6 ft; bottom 2 ft above groundwater and 5 ft above rock; 100 ft down gradient of water; alternate pairs daily
entries.dim: Depth 4-6 ft (max 6); bottom >=2 ft above groundwater, >=5 ft above rock; >=100 ft down gradient from water; spacing >=2x pit size; closure mound 1 ft above grade
entries.wn: A clogged pit will not accept liquid and must be properly closed

entries.desc: Used if groundwater/rock prevents digging a pit and 1.5 feet depth is acceptable. Central pit 2 feet square and 1 foot deep; a trench radiates outward from each side for 6 or more feet; trenches 1 foot wide, 1 foot deep at central pit increasing to 1.5 feet at outer end. Fill pit and trenches with gravel or broken rock. Build multiple units and alternate daily. Use grease trap for kitchen waste. Length varies with volume (seek technical guidance)
entries.use: Gray water where groundwater or rock prevents pits
entries.how: Central pit 2 ft square x 1 ft deep with 1-ft-wide trenches radiating 6+ ft, deepening from 1 ft to 1.5 ft; fill with gravel or broken rock
entries.dim: Central pit 2 ft x 2 ft x 1 ft deep; 4 trenches 6+ ft long x 1 ft wide, depth 1 ft to 1.5 ft

entries.n: Soakage area for hand-washing stations and lister bags
entries.desc: For outdoor devices such as hand-washing stations and lister bags: excavate underneath and a few inches out on all sides; fill holes with small stones. Receives only incidental drainage; not for gray water disposal
entries.use: Prevent mud/pooling under field water devices
entries.how: Excavate under and a few inches around the device and fill with small stones

entries.desc: Distribution of treated, recycled nonpotable water; piping is a shade of purple so it is never interconnected with potable lines. Gray water from showers, sinks, laundry can be treated and reused in toilets, irrigation/agriculture, firefighting, dust control, vehicle washing. Reuse criteria depend on location and HN agreements; PVNTMED must be consulted and approve. Toilets on purple pipe feed the black water system. ROWPU brine may be added with prior PVNTMED approval. Disinfected/filtered gray water may be reused for vehicle washing if PVNTMED approves; washrack settling basin can supply gravity-clarified water
entries.use: Reuse of gray water on a developed base camp
entries.how: Route shower, sink, laundry gray water to treatment and reuse for toilets, irrigation, firefighting, dust control, vehicle washing; PVNTMED must approve

entries.desc: Gray water from ROWPUs: brine wastewater, filter backwash wastewater, membrane cleaning wastewater; range from nonhazardous to hazardous. Nonhazardous options: wastewater treatment plant, brine wastewater lagoon, soakage pit/trench, possibly purple pipe. Do not discharge directly to an aerobic system used for black water (kills bacteria); do not discharge excess treated water directly to natural water systems (chlorine). Operators must know SDSs and wear PPE (hearing protection, face shield, chemical gloves, apron). Brine rates in Table 4-1
entries.use: Brine, backwash and membrane-cleaning wastewater
entries.how: Plan brine volumes by ROWPU size (Table 4-1); do not discharge to aerobic black-water lagoon or natural waters
entries.dim: See Table 4-1 (brine GPH by ROWPU)
entries.eq: PPE: hearing protection, face shield, chemical gloves, apron

entries.desc: Rates used: immediate 1.0 GPD/person (meal prep, mobile kitchen; negligible if field rations and wet wipes); basic 16 GPD/person; expanded 24 GPD/person; enhanced 40 GPD/person (ATP 3-37.10/MCRP 3-40D.13). Roughly 80 percent of all water used for purposes other than human consumption ends up as wastewater, generally gray water; most gray water from laundries, showers, dining facilities. Worked examples (Table 4-3): Battalion 700 x 1.0 = 700 GPD x 3 days = 2,100 gal; Battalion 700 x 24 = 16,800 GPD x 180 days = 3,024,000 gal; Company 100 x 1.0 = 100 GPD x 3 = 300 gal; Company 100 x 24 = 2,400 GPD x 180 = 432,000 gal. Force Provider: four 150-person modules collocated generate 20,000 gal/day gray water; each module gray water collection stores 40,000 gallons; Shower Water Reuse System recycles 75 percent of discarded shower water
entries.use: Estimating gray water gallons per day
entries.how: Immediate 1 gal/person/day; basic 16; expanded 24; enhanced 40 GPD/person. About 80 percent of non-drinking water becomes wastewater
entries.dim: Immediate 1 gal/person/day; basic 16; expanded 24; enhanced 40; ~80% of non-drinking water becomes wastewater; Force Provider 4 x 150-person modules = 20,000 gal/day; 40,000 gal storage per module; shower reuse 75%

entries.n: Latrine siting and general construction rules
entries.desc: Latrines at least 100 meters (~300 feet) downwind (prevailing wind) and down gradient from food service facilities; at least 30 meters (~100 feet) from nearest water source; usually at least 30 meters downwind from billeting and work areas, with equal access to users. Chemical/containerized latrines and holding tanks must be reachable by service vehicles. Do not contaminate groundwater or a water source; find groundwater table from geospatial data, local inhabitants or by digging until water reached. Light latrines at night if tactical situation permits or stake off with rope/tape. Screen with canvas or brush or enclose in tent; heat in cold climates. Drainage ditch to keep surface drainage out or contain overflow. Place a hand-washing device with constant water supply at each latrine on a soakage area. Clean latrines daily with disinfectant or soap and water; assign responsibility; notify field sanitation team of pests
entries.use: Locating any latrine
entries.how: Latrines at least 100 m downwind/down gradient of food service, at least 30 m from water sources and 30 m downwind of billeting/work areas
entries.dim: Latrines >=100 m (~300 ft) downwind/down gradient from food service; >=30 m (~100 ft) from water; ~30 m downwind from billeting/work areas
entries.eq: Disinfectant or soap and water, hand-washing device

entries.desc: To determine number of toilets: multiply total number of males by 4 percent (0.04) and total number of females by 6 percent (0.06), rounding up to the nearest whole number for each. Examples (Table 4-5): Battalion 700 (500 male, 200 female) = 20 male, 12 female latrines; Company 100 (80 male, 20 female) = 4 male, 2 female latrines. Force Provider: four 150-person modules collocated may generate 3,000 gallons of black water per day. Where stationary more than 72 hours (3 days), some field methods are unsuitable; transition to more sustainable methods
entries.use: Number of toilets needed
entries.how: Number of latrines = males x 0.04 plus females x 0.06, each rounded up
entries.dim: Males x 4%; females x 6%; round up; 500M/200F = 20/12; 80M/20F = 4/2

entries.desc: Simplest field-expedient method. Dug at least 1 foot square and 1 foot deep. After use, removed dirt is replaced and packed down. Alternative for short halts: commercially available disposable human waste bag
entries.use: Individuals on the move or stationary 1-3 days with no facilities
entries.how: Dig at least 1 ft square and 1 ft deep; replace and pack down dirt after use
entries.dim: At least 1 ft x 1 ft x 1 ft deep

entries.desc: Most common latrine for units stationary 1 to 3 days. Trench 1 foot wide, 2 1/2 feet deep, 4 feet long; one trench accommodates two persons at once. Trenches parallel and at least 2 feet apart. Excavated dirt piled at end of trench with shovel or paddle so users cover excreta and toilet paper. Boards along both sides for footing. Toilet paper on holders protected from weather by tin can or other cover. Close per latrine closure procedure
entries.use: Units stationary 1 to 3 days
entries.how: Dig trench 1 ft wide, 2.5 ft deep, 4 ft long for two persons; parallel trenches at least 2 ft apart
entries.dim: Trench 1 ft wide x 2.5 ft deep x 4 ft long; 2 persons; trenches >=2 ft apart
entries.eq: Shovel or paddle, boards, excavation equipment

entries.n: Deep pit latrine with four-seat box
entries.desc: Standard four-seat latrine box: 8 feet long, 2 1/2 feet wide at base, 18 inches high, installed over excavation. Pit dug 2 feet wide and 7 1/2 feet long (allows 3 inches of ground surface to support box on all sides). Depth guide: 1 foot per week of estimated use by 50 personnel plus 1 foot for dirt cover at closure; a 6-foot pit lasts about five weeks (depends on users). Pit no more than 6 feet deep (wall collapse); plank/shore if needed. Pack dirt tightly around box bottom edges to seal flies out; flyproof lids, flyproof cracks with wood/tin strips; fly control program. Scrub box and seats daily with soap and water. Use until filled to within 1 foot of top, then close
entries.use: Basic latrine operations for a few weeks
entries.how: Pit 2 ft x 7.5 ft; depth 1 ft per week per 50 personnel plus 1 ft cover; max 6 ft deep; box 8 ft x 2.5 ft x 18 in
entries.dim: Pit 2 ft x 7.5 ft; depth 1 ft per week per 50 persons + 1 ft; max 6 ft; 6 ft deep ~5 weeks; box 8 ft x 2.5 ft x 18 in
entries.eq: Four-seat latrine box, planking, flyproof lids
entries.wn: Lime or burning of pit contents does not effectively control flies or odor

entries.desc: Hole about 18 inches in diameter and 15 to 20 feet deep, dug with engineer equipment with auger attachment (diameter based on largest auger available). Covered by one-hole latrine box using a metal drum with both ends removed sunk in the ground; flyproof seat cover and lid. If no drum, flyproof wooden box 18 inches high. Use until filled to within 1 foot of top, then close properly
entries.use: Quick latrine where engineer auger is available
entries.how: Auger about 18 in. diameter and 15-20 ft deep, cover with one-hole box on drum; close at 1 ft from top
entries.dim: About 18 in. diameter x 15-20 ft deep; box 18 in. high
entries.eq: Engineer auger, drum, flyproof seat cover and lid

entries.desc: 55-gallon drum in the ground with enough aboveground for comfortable sitting height (for example 18 inches); may be cut in half for two lower-capacity latrines. Flyproof wooden seat with self-closing lid; weld handles so two persons can carry the drum since it must be moved before contents are burned. Have two sets of drums, one in use while other burned out. Men urinate in a separate urine facility (liquid needs more fuel). Burn contents daily, wearing PPE, with enough fuel to incinerate completely; do not use highly volatile fuel (gasoline) alone; use unserviceable fuel before serviceable vehicle fuel; a mixture of 1 quart gasoline to 4 quarts JP-8 or diesel is effective. Burn again if not dry and odorless; bury remaining ash. Burn downwind of base camp
entries.use: Where digging is impossible (high water table, rock, frozen ground)
entries.how: Sink a 55-gallon drum with about 18 in. above ground; burn contents daily with 1 qt gasoline to 4 qt JP-8/diesel; have two drum sets
entries.dim: Drum ~18 in. above ground; fuel mix 1 qt gasoline : 4 qt JP-8/diesel
entries.eq: 55-gallon drums (2 sets), flyproof seat, fuel, PPE
entries.wn: Fill drums with water before cutting to prevent explosion of residual fumes; gasoline alone is explosive; burn downwind of camp

entries.desc: Pit built in a mound above ground. Mound at least 6 feet wide and 12 feet long on top, supporting a four-seat box; high enough to meet pit depth requirement with a 1-foot buffer between pit base and groundwater table or rock. Scarify or plow the area for seepage. With timber, build a crib to enclose the pit and support the box; build mound by compacting each successive 1-foot layer up to top of crib, roughening (raking) each layer. Without timber, build mound in 1-foot layers and dig pit into it; brace walls with wood, sandbags etc. Enclose and flyproof like deep pit latrine
entries.use: High groundwater or rock prevents digging
entries.how: Build mound at least 6 ft x 12 ft on top in 1-ft compacted layers to hold a four-seat box; leave 1-ft buffer above groundwater/rock
entries.dim: Mound top at least 6 ft x 12 ft; 1-ft compacted layers; 1-ft buffer above groundwater/rock

entries.desc: Four-seat latrine box modified with hinged doors on rear, floor, and a pail under each seat. If in building/tent, position as part of outer wall so rear door opens from outside. Flyproof, self-closing seats and rear doors; impervious floor (concrete if possible) sloped to rear for washing water drainage. Plastic bag liners in pails; tie filled bags. Reuse plastic transport barrels to haul bags, cleaning and sanitizing between uses. Waste burned or hauled to burial/other disposal. Clean pails at least daily. Separate urine facilities for male latrines
entries.use: Where digging is impossible, or inside buildings
entries.how: Four-seat box with hinged rear doors, floor and a pail under each seat; clean pails at least daily; burn or bury bagged waste
entries.dim: Four-seat box; clean pails at least daily
entries.eq: Four-seat box, pails, plastic liners, barrels

entries.desc: Black water can be stored in chemical toilets or holding tanks until connection/transport to treatment facility. Chemicals (formaldehyde, bleach) can interfere with treatment; confirm facility accepts the waste. Preferable in the field when contractors available. Clean daily; empty frequency based on usage. Contracts must stipulate requirements and be inspected, including subcontractor disposal. Holding tanks/bladders must be clearly labeled with their contents to avoid confusion with potable water bladders. Force Provider containerized latrines use 3,000-gallon tanks; four 150-person modules collocated generate 3,000 gal black water/day; each module has an evacuation tank/trailer; Force Provider sustains deployments of 45 days to 2 years and will not be transferred to HN
entries.use: Black water storage until connection or hauling
entries.how: Clean daily, pump out for disposal to approved sewage system, verify contractor disposal; label holding tanks clearly
entries.dim: Force Provider latrine tank 3,000 gal; 4 x 150-person modules = 3,000 gal/day black water; deployments 45 days to 2 years
entries.eq: Chemical toilets, holding tanks, tank trucks
entries.wn: Label black water tanks to avoid confusion with potable bladders

entries.desc: Small treatment systems combining aeration, settling and solids treatment in a single multi-compartment tank; types include extended aeration, complete mix, step aeration, contact stabilization, biofiltration, rotating biological contactors, sequencing batch reactors. Not typically desirable with flows greater than 0.5 million gallons per day (0.022 m3/s). Needs specialized engineer/contractor support to install, maintain and operate; complex and not normally transferred to HN
entries.use: Sustainable base camps with engineer/contractor support
entries.how: Small modular plants; not desirable above 0.5 million gal/day; civil engineer must determine viability
entries.dim: Not desirable above 0.5 million gal/day (0.022 m3/s)

entries.desc: Engineered earthen basins where soil/wastewater bacteria digest organics and pathogens die off; typically meets discharge criteria except in cold regions. Requires civil engineering expertise (get via higher HQ or USACE/NAVFAC reachback), significant land area, and minimized absorption into soil through compaction and/or clay or membrane liner. Locate downwind at least half a mile from any populated area. Diverting gray water significantly reduces load. Design may use parallel basins or series of two to three consecutive basins; sand filter or wetland zone at effluent end; effluent may be reclaimed for agriculture if PVNTMED approves. Pumper trucks can dump sewage to lagoon instead of piping/lift stations. Suitable to turn over to HN; easy to maintain
entries.use: Constructed black water treatment, transferable to HN
entries.how: Engineered earthen basin(s) sited downwind at least half a mile from populated area, compacted or lined; use 2-3 basins in series
entries.dim: At least 0.5 mile downwind of populated areas; 2-3 basins in series
entries.eq: Earthmoving equipment, clay or membrane liner
entries.wn: Poorly built/managed lagoons can produce very foul odors

entries.desc: Design only by licensed experienced engineer. Septic tank settles solids (anaerobic digestion); effluent flows to drain field of buried perforated pipes (lateral lines) for aerobic digestion in soil. Preferred tank: precast concrete or fiberglass sized for volume, or concrete built in place. Empty every 3 to 5 years, or sooner if more than 1 foot of solids/sludge accumulates. Drain field conditions: topography allows proper pipe slope; groundwater table well below drain field; soil can absorb the volume; at least 300 feet between drain field and any existing drinking water source, with negligible contamination risk (particularly shallow or driven wells). Traffic limited to avoid crushing pipes. A pump may dose effluent to the drain field, letting it drain and rest between doses
entries.use: Black water treatment/disposal by tank and leach field
entries.how: Precast concrete or fiberglass tank; empty every 3-5 years or when more than 1 ft of sludge; drain field at least 300 ft from drinking water
entries.dim: Tank emptied every 3-5 years or >1 ft sludge; drain field >=300 ft from drinking water

entries.desc: Allow at least 1 foot of space between contents and top of pit. Spray contents, side walls, and ground surface to 2 feet from side walls with approved insecticide. Fill to ground level with successive 3-inch layers of compacted dirt; spray each layer with DOD-approved insecticide before next layer. Cover pit with 1-foot mound of compacted dirt. Mark with rectangular sign marked 'CLOSED LATRINE' with date and unit; document 8-digit grid in closure reports
entries.use: Closing a latrine pit or trench
entries.how: Leave 1 ft below rim, spray insecticide, fill in 3-in. compacted layers with insecticide between layers, 1-ft mound, post CLOSED LATRINE sign, record 8-digit grid
entries.dim: Leave >=1 ft; spray out to 2 ft from walls; 3 in. compacted layers; 1 ft mound; 8-digit grid
entries.wn: Local requirements may vary; HN agreements may require more detailed methods or monitoring

entries.desc: Pump out tank and dispose of contents; disconnect sanitary line; remove or crush top; break tank bottom open so it will not hold runoff; fill with stone, rubble, or soil after required inspections; mark with rectangular sign (contents, date filled, unit); document 8-digit grid in closure reports
entries.use: Closing a septic tank
entries.how: Pump out, disconnect sanitary line, crush top, break bottom, fill with stone/rubble/soil, mark and record 8-digit grid
entries.dim: 8-digit grid

entries.n: Wastewater facility closure at base camp transfer
entries.desc: Facilities properly closed and marked identifying contents and date. Methods generally cover and compact with dirt; HN agreements may require more detailed methods and long-term groundwater monitoring. In absence of formal guidance use best management practices, possibly environmental experts. Seek assistance from higher HQ, USACE and PVNTMED teams
entries.use: Closing latrines, soakage pits/trenches, lagoons, septic systems
entries.how: Close and mark all wastewater facilities with contents and date; follow HN agreements; use best management practices if no guidance

entries.n: Classify HAZMAT, HW and special waste
entries.desc: HAZMAT supplied with an SDS; becomes HW if it can no longer be used (expiration, contamination, spillage) or is hazardous as generated waste. HW: solid waste listed in federal law or exhibiting ignitability, corrosiveness, reactivity or toxicity (e.g., used solvents, waste fuel filters, contaminated fuel, paint waste, nonpunctured aerosol cans, petroleum-contaminated dirt). Special waste examples: used POL, used antifreeze, asbestos-containing materials, black water sludge, petroleum-contaminated dirt, incinerator ash, spill cleanup debris. Unknown composition must be tested. Do not automatically classify expired-shelf-life HAZMAT as HW; first try to extend shelf life (DOD Shelf-Life Program). Containers with less than one year remaining shelf life should not be shipped into contingency locations. Do not designate usable HAZMAT as HW just to clean up
entries.use: Deciding what stream a material belongs in
entries.how: HW = listed or ignitable/corrosive/reactive/toxic; special waste = non-HW needing special handling; unknown material must be tested
entries.dim: HAZMAT shipped with at least 1 year shelf life remaining

entries.n: Hazardous waste accumulation point (HWAP) siting and operation
entries.desc: Locate HWAPs and HWSAs at least 100 meters from any water resource, inhabited-building distance from ammunition supply points, down gradient and downwind of billeting and dining; away from flame sources and heavy traffic; flat level ground, not flood-prone; controlled access; spills must not reach surface water/drains; near roads for vehicle access. Size from anticipated accumulation; ample aisle space for personnel, handling, firefighting, decon and spill equipment. HWAP at/near point of generation; one may suffice at small camps. Generator is responsible for accumulation and housekeeping: no mixing of streams, only approved waste in container, secondary containment, respond to/record/report spills, clean small leaks with absorbent and manage as HW, segregate by hazard, do not overfill, avoid rupture. As a rule in contingency locations, once a container is full the generator arranges transport. HWSA is last in-theater stop, usually under DLA or qualified contractor; no volume/time limits if storage requirements met
entries.use: Setting up a unit HW collection point
entries.how: Place at or near point of generation, at least 100 m from water, flat ground, downwind/down gradient of billeting and dining, access controlled
entries.dim: HWAP/HWSA at least 100 m from any water resource
entries.wn: Unknown waste must be sampled and characterized before entering HWSA

entries.desc: Cover and protect HWAPs/HWSAs to keep rain out of accumulation and secondary containment and avoid sun exposure; tarps are temporary expedient if secure. Control access by 24-hour monitoring or barriers (signs, rope, yellow and black tape, fencing) not blocking material handling/emergency vehicles. Post NFPA or applicable international warning signs. Signs on all sides: 'HAZARDOUS WASTE ACCUMULATION POINT (or HAZARDOUS WASTE STORAGE AREA) - DANGER UNAUTHORIZED PERSONNEL KEEP OUT' and 'NO SMOKING WITHIN 50 FEET' in English and prominent local language; legible from at least 25 feet; include contact information
entries.use: Securing a hazardous waste site
entries.how: Cover from rain/sun, control access 24 hr or with barriers, sign on all sides with NO SMOKING WITHIN 50 FEET
entries.dim: Sign legible from at least 25 ft; no smoking within 50 ft

entries.n: Secondary containment sizing for HW containers
entries.desc: Secondary containment required for all waste containers. Capacity must hold the greater of 10 percent of the total volume contained or 100 percent of the single largest container, plus freeboard for precipitation and expansion (general rule add extra 10 percent). Example: eight 55-gallon drums: 10 percent of total = 44 gal (8 x 55 x 0.10); largest container = 55 gal; greater is 55 gal; add 10 percent (5.5 gal) = 60.5-gallon containment. Types: plastic tubs, sumps, curbed concrete pads, spill control pallets, plastic-lined pits/trenches/dikes/berms. Field expedient: place containers on large plastic tarp with filled sandbags stacked around perimeter and tarp edges draped over sandbags. Provide overhead cover; inspect/test collected rainwater before release; contaminated rainwater is HW. Upgrade to concrete hardstands as theater matures
entries.use: Preventing spread of spills and leaks from waste containers
entries.how: Capacity = greater of 10 percent of total volume or 100 percent of largest container, plus about 10 percent freeboard
entries.dim: Greater of 10% of total volume or 100% of largest container, plus ~10% freeboard (8 x 55 gal drums -> 60.5 gal)

entries.n: HW storage segregation (reactive, ignitable, corrosive, toxic)
entries.desc: Initially segregate into reactives, ignitables, corrosives, toxics (Table 5-3), then by compatibility per SDS. Avoid: reactives with ignitables; acids (pH<7) with bases (pH>7); corrosives with ignitables; oxidizers with everything; organic reactives with inorganic reactives. Compressed gas cylinders not with flammable special waste. Separate each storage section by 6 feet or by a physical barrier (earthen/HESCO berm or T walls). Where possible locate ignitable/reactive storage at least 50 feet inside camp boundary. Post 'NO SMOKING WITHIN 50 FEET' and ground all metal containers. See TM 38-410
entries.use: Laying out storage inside HWAP/HWSA
entries.how: Four sections; separate each by 6 ft or a physical barrier; keep acids from bases and oxidizers from everything
entries.dim: Sections separated by 6 ft or barrier; ignitable/reactive storage at least 50 ft inside boundary

entries.n: HWAP emergency equipment and spill kit
entries.desc: Posted spill response plan (responsibilities, notification, reporting, POCs), rehearsed. Equipment: spill kits compatible with HW on site; at a minimum a HWAP should have approximately 15 pounds of absorbent, two nonsparking shovels, two brooms, plastic bags for contaminated absorbent; HWSAs more. ABC-type fire extinguishers; potable water for eye washing and decon; four sets of appropriate PPE (two for cleanup, two for backup team); emergency communication or alarm device
entries.use: Minimum emergency gear at a hazardous waste site
entries.how: HWAP minimum: ~15 lb absorbent, two nonsparking shovels, two brooms, plastic bags, ABC extinguishers, eyewash water, four PPE sets, alarm
entries.dim: ~15 lb absorbent; 2 nonsparking shovels; 2 brooms; 4 PPE sets (2 cleanup, 2 backup)
entries.eq: Spill kit, absorbents (Table 5-1), ABC extinguishers, PPE (Table 5-4)

entries.desc: Environmental officer inspects at least weekly; waste generators inspect assigned areas daily; correct deficiencies immediately; root cause analysis for noncompliance. Inspection record: date and time, inspector, observations, date and nature of corrective actions. HWSAs inspected by DLA or COR. Recordkeeping: accurate inventory and storage duration, log of type, quantity, date, generating unit; per-container record that travels with container; manager completes DD Form 1348-1A and DLA Form 2511; keep training records. HW management records kept at least 3 years (or as set by CCDR); provide to incoming unit at transfer. Report 8-digit grid and inventories to higher; load inventories in DOEHRS-Environmental Health
entries.use: Compliance of accumulation points
entries.how: Generators inspect daily, environmental officer at least weekly, keep records 3 years
entries.dim: Records at least 3 years; generator inspection daily; EO inspection at least weekly

entries.desc: Prefer steel or polyethylene containers meeting UN requirements; best is original shipping container if closable and transport-approved. Grounded steel drums for toxic and ignitable waste; polyethylene for corrosive acids, bases and oxidizers; corrosives only in plastic or plastic-lined containers. Any other container must be in good condition (no severe rust, bulges, dents, holes), compatible, closable and transport-approved. Remove or paint over old labels on reused containers. Keep closed when not adding/removing. Headspace for liquids: approximately 4 inches in a 55-gallon drum, 2 inches in a 5-gallon container, 1 inch in a 1-gallon container; double in extremely hot climates (desert). Use funnels, remove them (unless self-closing) after transfer. Use nonsparking tools and grounded metal containers for ignitables. Small work-area containers labeled with chemical name and hazard, used for one waste stream, emptied into HWAP container at end of each shift. See Table 5-2 for NSNs
entries.use: Packaging hazardous and special waste
entries.how: Use original container or UN-approved steel/polyethylene; steel for toxic/ignitable, plastic for corrosives; leave 4 in. headspace in 55-gal drum
entries.dim: Headspace 4 in. (55 gal), 2 in. (5 gal), 1 in. (1 gal); double in desert
entries.eq: Containers per Table 5-2, funnels, nonsparking tools

entries.desc: Each container marked with contents (e.g., 'used oil', 'contaminated soil'), hazards (e.g., 'ignitable'), generating unit designation or UIC, 'Hazardous Waste', and the date waste is first placed in the container (accumulation start); re-date when transferred to HWSA or as directed by theater SOP. Use indelible paint pen or stencils in English and predominant local language. Lettering at least one inch in size in contrasting color, visible from a distance. Arrange containers with markings facing outward
entries.use: Labeling waste containers
entries.how: Mark contents, hazard, generating unit, 'Hazardous Waste' and accumulation start date; letters at least 1 in., indelible, facing outward
entries.dim: Lettering at least 1 inch

entries.desc: SDSs required at HAZMAT and HW storage areas, refueling sites, maintenance facilities and MTFs; each brand has its own SDS; check date of manufacture. If missing: manufacturer website/email, DLA HMIRS (if NSN), or environmental officer. Binders available on site; update at least every 5 years and when new SDS issued. HW and special waste generally have no SDS unless unused or pure HAZMAT; HW requires laboratory analysis for characterization; generator knowledge may be used if waste previously analyzed, occurs often, same process; reanalyze if process/products change
entries.use: Identifying hazards of materials and waste
entries.how: Keep SDS binders at HAZMAT/HW storage, refueling, maintenance, MTF; update at least every 5 years; HW needs lab analysis for definitive characterization
entries.dim: SDS updated at least every 5 years

entries.desc: PPE is primary protection; evaluate need before handling; check SDSs. Decontaminate or dispose of contaminated PPE promptly; characterize contaminated PPE for HW. Respirators only for personnel with pulmonary fitness test and fit test by PVNTMED or trained personnel; no universal cartridge. HWAP/HWSA operators may need fully encapsulating suits. Individual protective equipment (field gloves, goggles, wet-weather gear) only when required PPE is unavailable. Table 5-4 NSNs include acid-resistant rubber apron, oil-resistant plastic apron, heat-protective gloves, synthetic rubber and butyl rubber gloves, portable eyewash, eyewash solution, emergency drench shower, face shield, goggles
entries.use: Selecting protective equipment
entries.how: Check SDS; respirators only for fit-tested, pulmonary-tested personnel; use IPE only when PPE unavailable

entries.desc: Transport from unit/camp HWAPs to theater HWSA (treatment/disposal by DLA or qualified contractors). Package per FGS, HN or international shipping standards. Drivers certified for hazardous cargo (via transportation unit); vehicles approved, with placards, manifests, copy of spill response plan. Vehicle equipment: spill kit with approximately 25 pounds of absorbent, two nonsparking picks, two nonsparking shovels, one broom, small and large heavy-plastic bags; ABC extinguisher; potable water for eyewash/decon; two sets of PPE; communication. Personnel signing shipping documents must complete approved certification. Forms: DD Form 2890, DD Form 1348-1A, DD Form 1348-2, DA Form 3161, bill of lading, HN forms. Vehicles that carried radioactive waste must be surveyed by RSO/CBRN personnel and cleared before other use. Special requirements for military aircraft
entries.use: Moving HW from HWAP to HWSA
entries.how: Certified drivers, approved placarded vehicle, spill plan and kit (~25 lb absorbent, 2 picks, 2 shovels, broom), manifests
entries.dim: ~25 lb absorbent per vehicle; 2 nonsparking picks; 2 nonsparking shovels; 1 broom; 2 PPE sets
entries.eq: Placards, manifests, spill kit, ABC extinguisher

entries.n: Used oil / fuel blending and reuse
entries.desc: Used-oil blenders collect used oil from a diesel engine crankcase (diesel only), collect an equal amount of fuel from the tank, blend, filter, and pump back as fuel; avoids collection, storage, transport and disposal cost. Consult maintenance personnel first. Unusable oil may go via government contract to local vendors as fuel (environmental officer verifies and documents). If authorized by SOP, blend oils with diesel as accelerants in incinerators with proper tanks. Consolidated HAZMAT storage/reuse issue facility for paint, POL, solvents; substitute nonhazardous materials; use oldest shelf-life first
entries.use: Reducing used oil and HAZMAT waste
entries.how: Blend used diesel-engine oil with fuel using a used-oil blender; reuse paint, POL, solvents through a HAZMAT reuse issue facility
entries.dim: Blend ratio: equal amount of fuel to used oil (1:1)
entries.wn: Only used oil from diesel engines

entries.desc: Primary disposal is through a qualified contractor or DLA facility in theater; local contracts approved through chain of command. If not possible, transport to DLA facility or HWSA in theater. Units may never incinerate or bury HW (and certain special waste) unless explicitly approved by both U.S. and HN authorities. Comply with FGS, HN regulations, DOD 4715.05-G, international shipping rules. DLA provides forms, training, identification help and lab analysis. Treatment options to reduce hazard: biodegradation, chemical degradation, stabilization/fixation, neutralization of corrosives, composition changes, with approval from higher HQ, APHC, DLA
entries.use: Final disposition of HW and special waste
entries.how: Disposal is by DLA or qualified contractor; never incinerate or bury HW without US and HN approval
entries.wn: Never burn or bury HW without approval

entries.desc: Used lead-acid, nickel-cadmium, mercury, lithium, silver and magnesium batteries usually HW; do not comingle types; tape off terminals if needed. Lead-acid batteries may be palletized if protected from weather and damage, not stacked more than two high; recycle (often one-for-one exchange). Magnesium batteries emit hydrogen gas: not in airtight containers; once 50 percent depleted they become solid waste. Alkaline batteries are not HW and may be landfilled; if trash is burned, collect alkaline and magnesium separately (bursting hazard). See TB 43-0134
entries.use: Used batteries
entries.how: Lead-acid, NiCd, mercury, lithium, silver, magnesium are generally HW; palletize lead-acid no more than two high; do not mix types
entries.dim: Lead-acid stack max two high; magnesium batteries nonhazardous when 50% depleted

entries.desc: Aerosol cans: intact = reactive HW. Local policy may allow commercial puncturing device to capture contents; use a separate puncturing system per waste stream (e.g., paint vs. pesticide); verify residue is not HW; punctured cans may be recycled as scrap. Paint aerosol cans: puncture and drain into paint waste container, dry, then scrap metal or trash; never general refuse unpunctured. Lamps (fluorescent, HID, neon, mercury vapor, sodium vapor, metal halide): collect in protective sleeves/boxes and recycle; if broken, ventilate, sweep into sealed plastic bag; broken mercury bulbs are HW. Ballasts: assume PCB content unless marked as electronic non-PCB; dispose via DLA
entries.use: Handling common small HW items
entries.how: Intact aerosol cans are reactive HW; puncture only with a commercial puncturing device per waste stream; recycle lamps; assume old ballasts contain PCBs

entries.desc: Fuel spills are the most common source of HW during a deployment (see appendix C). Treatment options: incinerate, bioremediate, land farm, encapsulate, or excavate and containerize for shipment to a treatment facility (consult DLA or theater command). Small spill soil and absorbent are shoveled into leakproof containers (heavy plastic bags, drums, plastic-lined containers) and taken to designated collection facility/HWAP for petroleum-contaminated dirt. Petroleum-contaminated dirt should be bioremediated on-site per theater SOP. Petroleum-contaminated dirt may be used as landfill cover
entries.use: Fuel spills (most common source of HW)
entries.how: Shovel small-spill soil and absorbent into leakproof containers for designated HW accumulation; options include bioremediation, land farming, incineration

entries.desc: Used oil and antifreeze are special waste; waste solvents, grease, dry sweep, used rags must be evaluated. Rags can be laundered/reused. Oil dry nonhazardous or special unless it absorbed hazardous material. Oil, fuel and other filters (not air filters) segregated; used oil filters gravity-drained with liquid and drained filter collected separately in metal drums; non-terne plated filters gravity hot-drained, crushed and recycled as scrap. CLP (e.g., Break Free) manufactured after March 1994 nonhazardous (rags can go in regular trash); before March 1994 needs waste characterization; weapons-cleaning waste checked for lead. Solvent tank cleaning yields three streams (spent solvent, tank-bottom sludge, solvent filter), each evaluated; if solvent hazardous all three are HW. Reduce solvent loss: let parts drain before removal ('drag out') and keep lids closed
entries.use: Motor pool waste streams
entries.how: Drain oil filters by gravity (hot), crush and recycle; evaluate solvents, sludge and filters as three separate streams

entries.n: Paint, pesticide, ration heater and calcium hypochlorite waste
entries.desc: Paint: return open containers to supply. Latex (water-based) not hazardous; small amounts may go to sanitary wastewater treatment (not septic) or be dried and trashed. Oil-based paint is HW (containerize) but becomes nonhazardous solid waste when dry; paint thinner is hazardous, may be combined with oil-based paint waste; CARC paint may be hazardous (heavy metals) unless water-based; verify characterization. Pesticides: follow label disposal instructions; plan quantity to use all; waste pesticide often HW; do not containerize with paint waste; personal-use pesticide empties go as solid waste after complete use, bulk expired is HW. Flameless ration heaters: small numbers regular trash; bulk unused quantities are reactive HW; activate with meal before disposal or reissue. Field sanitation team supplies including granular calcium hypochlorite: manage as HW; do not burn with trash or bury in landfills
entries.use: Misc. HW items
entries.how: Latex paint nonhazardous; oil-based paint and thinner are HW until dry; calcium hypochlorite is HW, never burn or landfill

entries.desc: Asbestos is toxic by inhalation and a carcinogen; found in pipe insulation, roofing and siding, floor tiles, brake shoes. Abatement by approved contractors or certified personnel. Waste is special waste. Wet and double-bag, seal with duct tape, or place in airtight container. Label: 'DANGER-CONTAINS ASBESTOS FIBERS-AVOID CREATING DUST-CANCER AND LUNG DISEASE HAZARD.'
