Disposal normally in approved landfill
entries.use: Asbestos-containing material
entries.how: Only certified personnel; wet, double-bag, seal with duct tape; label DANGER - CONTAINS ASBESTOS FIBERS
entries.dim: Double-bag
entries.wn: Do not create dust

entries.desc: Radioactive waste handled only by designated personnel (AR 700-48 or MCO 5104.3B); DLA does not manage it. Wear disposable gloves for small quantities of suspected low-level items (damaged tritium compasses, fire control azimuths, chemical-agent monitors); double-bag in plastic; mark 'SUSPECTED RADIOACTIVE WASTE'; do not remove items from bags until final destination; strict chain of custody (DA Form 4137); record names/units and exposure dates and give to radiation safety and medical personnel. CBRN: turn in used mask filters, protective garments, decon kits, detectors to unit CBRN NCO; seal suspected chemical/biological items in leakproof bags or drums as HW; bulk decontamination agents are corrosive HW
entries.use: Suspected radiological or CBRN items
entries.how: Double-bag, mark SUSPECTED RADIOACTIVE WASTE, keep chain of custody; seal CBRN items in leakproof bags or drums as HW

entries.desc: Leachate: all liquid draining from a landfill goes to a managed, secure leachate collection basin; never discharge to a water source; may be accepted by an industrial-capable wastewater plant (with approval) or recirculated onto waste surface; collection system must prevent soil infiltration and groundwater contamination; runoff contacting compost or residual waste also diverted to leachate collection/treatment. PCBs: toxic, persistent; all transformers considered PCB transformers unless information to the contrary; keep out of floor and storm drains; spill plan includes PCB equipment with written inventory; lab analysis (ppm) may be needed; package enclosed and nonleaking; dispose through DLA; label equipment with PCB ppm or PCB-free
entries.use: Landfill leachate; PCB equipment
entries.how: Route leachate to a secure collection basin; treat all transformers as PCB unless known otherwise

entries.desc: E-waste (computers, printers, fax machines, cell phones, televisions): collect and recycle via DLA Disposition Services; landfilling releases heavy metals, open burning releases dioxins/furans. Tires: store to minimize insects/rodents/fires; indoors if possible or under secured waterproof cover with aisle space for inspecting and purging water; include tire fires in emergency plans; reuse for tire walls of dams, fences, barriers; properly stacked, dirt-filled and stuccoed tires insulate and resist fire and insects; shred ASAP if shredder available for walkways, landfills, embankments, roadways; otherwise contact DLA
entries.use: Electronics and tires
entries.how: Recycle e-waste through DLA; store tires indoors or covered with aisle space, shred early, reuse for walls and barriers

entries.n: HW and special waste training requirements
entries.desc: Annual environmental awareness training for personnel at every level. Training before deployment and before appointing personnel to HAZMAT/HW duties, then annual refresher. Minimum: hazard communication (markings, labels, SDSs), HAZMAT handling/storage/use, emergency and spill response, HW training, environmental officer training. Recommended: risk management, transportation of HAZMAT/HW, disposal requirements, lead/asbestos awareness, safety, treatments. Resources: organic or supporting environmental office, USAES DEI Environmental Officer Course, APHC, DLA, ISEERB, CECOS
entries.use: Training handlers and managers
entries.how: Annual environmental awareness training; training before appointment and annual refresher
entries.dim: Annual refresher

entries.desc: Estimate by analyzing equipment density lists, HAZMAT inventories and activities. Equipment relying on batteries will be hazardous when discarded. Characterize each waste by physical, chemical and descriptive properties (ignitable, corrosive, reactive, toxic); keep HW SOP with HW profile sheet (DD Form 1348-1A and DLA Form 2511), updated when streams/processes change. Sample (Table 5-6) company: semiannual services for 100 HMMWVs (2 gallons engine oil twice/year) = 34 gallons used oil/month and 17 filters/month; resources: HWAP materials in motor pool, spill kits with absorbent, shovels, labels, containers/overpack, transport to HWSA, PPE, fire extinguisher. Tools: DLA HMIRS and APHC MIDI database
entries.use: Preliminary HW estimate for a unit
entries.how: List activities that generate HW, estimate amount and frequency from equipment density lists, HAZMAT inventories; watch battery-powered equipment
entries.dim: 100 HMMWVs x 2 gal engine oil twice/yr = 34 gal used oil/month and 17 filters/month

entries.n: HW and special waste closure timeline
entries.desc: Sixty days prior: initial coordination with environmental office for HW/special waste removal from HWAPs; coordinate preliminary (30 days out) and final (24 hours out) ESCS; conduct internal ESCS; request support beyond unit capability; ensure packaging supplies (approved containers, labels, placards, SDSs) and cleanup supplies. Thirty days prior: confirm final removal coordinated, conduct preliminary ESCS, resolve identified issues before final ESCS. Twenty-four hours prior: conduct final ESCS and resolve last-minute issues. Closure plan also covers HAZMAT disposition, packaging/labeling/turn-in of HW, equipment removal and cleanup, empty container turn-in, fuel bladders and secondary containment liners removal, berms. ESCR documents final condition and is completed before the unit is released; documents forwarded to CCDR for MESL
entries.use: Base camp transfer/closure
entries.how: T-60 days coordinate HW removal and ESCS; T-30 preliminary ESCS; T-24 hours final ESCS
entries.dim: 60 days, 30 days, 24 hours before closure/transfer

entries.desc: Medical waste = waste from diagnosis, treatment, research or immunization of humans or animals that may cause disease. Categories (Table 6-1): 1 Cultures, stocks, vaccines; 2 Pathological waste; 3 Blood and blood products (including items saturated/dripping or caked with dried blood capable of releasing blood; not sanitary products); 4 Used sharps; 5 Animal waste; 6 Isolation wastes (BSL-4); 7 Unused sharps; 8 Other fluids; 9 Chemotherapy trace wastes. Gloves, masks, dressings, bandages, catheters, swabs, drapes, gowns, diapers, empty specimen cups generally regular trash if not saturated. Syringes without needles not tainted with body fluids may be regular trash; unused noninfectious glass in 'broken glass' boxes. Theater surgeon designates whether nonbloody waste from unique local diseases is medical waste
entries.use: Identifying what counts as regulated medical waste
entries.how: Nine groups: cultures/vaccines, pathological, blood, used sharps, animal, isolation, unused sharps, other fluids, chemotherapy trace

entries.n: Collecting medical waste (red bags and sharps)
entries.desc: Medical personnel segregate at point of generation. Collect in red bags (or theater-specified color) at least 3 mils thick or meeting 165 gram Impact Strength ASTM D 1709-01 and 480 gram Tear Strength ASTM D1922-15. No ammunition, UXO or explosives in bags. Mark bags/receptacles with universal biohazard symbol and 'BIOHAZARD' in English and prevalent local language. Sharps in puncture-resistant, leak-resistant, uniquely colored/marked containers; expedients: rigid plastic or metal container (coffee can, plastic drink bottle), placed into red bags or sharps containers ASAP. Never compact medical waste; do not shake or squeeze bags to reduce volume. Use universal precautions (gloves, masks, aprons). Do not mix with hazardous or radioactive waste
entries.use: At the point of generation in a medical treatment facility
entries.how: Use red bags at least 3 mil with biohazard symbol; sharps in rigid puncture-resistant containers; never compact or squeeze bags
entries.dim: Bag thickness at least 3 mils; 165 g impact strength; 480 g tear strength
entries.wn: Never compact; do not mix medical with HW or radioactive waste

entries.desc: Store near medical units in access-controlled, ventilated area protected from sun, rain, pests; never with regular trash or HW; away from food and common areas; display biohazard symbol and 'BIOHAZARD'; log type, quantity and disposition. Freezer storage usual time approximately 30 days. Medical waste (other than sharps containers) not stored above 40 F for more than 5 days. Covered cargo trailer may serve if requirements met. Allocate space for supplies (spill kits, bags, sharps containers, drums, PPE, labels) and for generators and refrigeration for pathological waste. Records and documentation kept at least three years
entries.use: Holding medical waste before treatment/pickup
entries.how: Store in controlled, ventilated area away from food; freezer ~30 days; above 40 F no more than 5 days (except sharps containers)
entries.dim: Freezer ~30 days; max 5 days above 40 F; records 3 years

entries.desc: Medical waste is HAZMAT for transport (chapter 5 requirements). Military, government or contractor vehicles; secure to prevent excessive movement; not in the same vehicle as food; clean and disinfect vehicle before other use; trained drivers. Spill kit with PPE, disinfectant, absorbent material and equipment to gather residue
entries.use: Moving medical waste
entries.how: Treat as HAZMAT; secure load; never with food; clean and disinfect vehicle after; carry spill kit

entries.n: Medical waste treatment and disposal hierarchy
entries.desc: Contractors with training/equipment preferred; scopes of work precise; contracts based on weight (not volume) or number of containers; COR monitors; environmental officer and surgeon jointly inspect HN disposal facilities. Without contractors: hierarchy is high-temperature two-stage incineration, sterilization, retrograding, burial, or alternative technologies per theater guidance. Treated waste may go to clinical sinks only if connected to suitable wastewater plant after sterilization and with PVNTMED consultation and higher HQ approval. Pharmaceuticals: SB 8-75-11 and APHC MIDI database
entries.use: Choosing a medical waste disposal method
entries.how: Use contractors first (priced by weight or container count); otherwise high-temp two-stage incineration, sterilization, retrograde, burial

entries.desc: Preferred method: approved medical waste incinerator. Open burning prohibited unless no alternative, with approval by geographic combatant commander and inclusion in theater solid waste management plan. Conduct as far downwind as possible (at least 450 feet) from inhabited areas. Commercial incinerator minimum burn temperature 1,500 F for at least 1 hour. Berm or fence with warning signs. Trained operators (operation, maintenance, safety, PPE, emergency response). Test bottom ash and air pollution control ash for HW properties before landfilling; hazardous ash managed as HW. Never incinerate aerosol cans, gas cylinders, batteries or other explosive hazards. Seek chain-of-command approval before using field-expedient devices
entries.use: Preferred medical waste destruction
entries.how: Approved incinerator with minimum 1,500 F for at least 1 hour, sited at least 450 ft downwind, fenced; test ash
entries.dim: At least 450 ft downwind; minimum 1,500 F for at least 1 hour
entries.wn: Never incinerate aerosol cans, gas cylinders, batteries

entries.desc: Best available field-expedient means (see TM56-3-15); handles waste for a combat support hospital or similar-size unit. Waste feed approximately 10 percent by weight medical waste (including sharps) to 90 percent regular trash. Avoid burning when wind blows smoke toward camp. Ash without sharps and evaluated nonhazardous may be buried with solid waste; hazardous ash managed as HW; nonhazardous ash containing sharps goes in 55-gallon drums retrograded to approved landfill (not a HAZMAT shipment). If retrograde of sharps not possible, bury below scavenger depth (approximately 8 feet), preferably with sterilization or grinding. Operators wear skin protection and air-purifying respirator (cartridge/canister) with HEPA filter; paper surgical masks and personal protective masks are not substitutes. Alternative sharps method: sharps management system (add two chemicals; contents solidify; then nonhazardous solid waste)
entries.use: Field-expedient destruction of medical waste including sharps
entries.how: Feed about 10 percent medical waste to 90 percent regular trash by weight; wear HEPA air-purifying respirator; bury ash with sharps below 8 ft
entries.dim: 10% medical : 90% regular trash by weight; bury sharps ash below ~8 ft; 55-gal drums
entries.eq: Inclined-plane burner, 55-gallon drums, HEPA air-purifying respirator
entries.wn: Paper surgical masks do not protect

entries.desc: Secure waste in autoclave bags (regular plastic may melt); use indicator tape; follow manufacturer time/temperature. After cooling, manage as regular trash (take care to prevent needle sticks). Field sterilizers used for waste never used for medical items and permanently marked 'FOR MEDICAL WASTE ONLY - DO NOT USE FOR STERILIZATION'. Have contingency plan (field sterilizers break down). Test autoclaves weekly using bacterial spores (DOD 4715.05-G). Table 6-2 products: autoclavable biohazard bags 26x18 in. (200/pkg) and 36x24 in. (100/pkg), sharps containers, spore strips, disinfectants, portable counter-top sterilizers inside 16x26x16 in. and 20x38x20 in
entries.use: Alternative to incineration
entries.how: Use autoclave bags and indicator tape; test weekly with spore strips; sterilizer marked FOR MEDICAL WASTE ONLY
entries.dim: Weekly spore test; sterilizers 16 x 26 x 16 in. and 20 x 38 x 20 in
entries.eq: Autoclave bags, indicator tape, spore strips

entries.desc: Last resort: bury untreated medical waste in a sanitary landfill in an area with deep groundwater table. Bury below 8 feet to prevent scavenging. Optional layer of lime over waste for decomposition and chemical disinfection. Mark site and report grid locations through chain of command in case recovery needed. If incinerator/sterilizer unavailable, retrograde to a sustainment area with facilities, coordinated with higher HQ per international agreements
entries.use: When no incinerator, sterilizer or retrograde
entries.how: Bury below 8 ft in sanitary landfill with deep water table; optional lime layer; mark and report grid
entries.dim: Below 8 ft depth

entries.desc: Closure plan covers removal or disposition of unused/reusable medical products, supplies and equipment; treatment of medical waste to allow disposal as solid waste; containerizing, inventorying, labeling and turning in medical waste; removal of medical equipment and site work
entries.use: Base camp transfer/closure for medical waste
entries.how: Plan removal of unused products, treat waste for disposal, containerize/inventory/label/turn in, remove equipment

entries.n: Waste stream classification into six types
entries.desc: Identify waste by unit function (Figure A-1), then use waste classification flowchart (Figure A-2) and wastewater flowchart (Figure A-3) to place into one of six types: nonhazardous solid waste (ch 3), gray water (ch 4), black water (ch 4), HW (ch 5), special waste (ch 5), medical waste (ch 6). Flowchart contents are graphical and not reproduced in the text extract
entries.use: Sorting a waste item into its stream
entries.how: Classify every item as nonhazardous solid, gray water, black water, HW, special waste or medical waste using the Appendix A flowcharts
entries.src: TM 3-34.56 Appendix A, para A-1, A-2

entries.desc: Appendix to engineer or sustainment annex. Para 1 Situation (terrain, weather, enemy, friendly, civil, attachments, assumptions); 2 Mission; 3 Execution (scheme of support with priorities of effort/support per phase, tasks to subordinate units, coordinating instructions: health risk measures, pollution prevention, collection/accumulation sites, disposition instructions, RFIs, reachback channels, information dissemination); 4 Sustainment (stockage levels/basic loads of PPE, containers, spill materials; ordering and contracting channels); 5 Command and Signal. Sample tasks: AA Patriot (immediate): construct field-expedient latrines, prepare closure plan; FOB Baker (basic): contract chemical latrines for 600 males and 200 females for a minimum of 90 days; Camp Lancer (expanded): establish HWAP per TM 3-34.56 and UFC 4-440-01 and disseminate grid and transport procedures. Do not repeat SOP content
entries.use: Writing waste tasks into an OPLAN/OPORD
entries.how: Put a waste management appendix in the engineer or sustainment annex: situation, mission, execution tasks by unit and category, sustainment stockage, command and signal
entries.dim: Sample: chemical latrines for 600 males and 200 females, minimum 90 days

entries.n: Spill prevention C-H-E-C-K for storage and accumulation sites
entries.desc: Containment: secondary containment in good condition, drain water regularly, dispose of sheen water as HW. Locations: appropriate sites, warning signs, clean and orderly. Environmental documentation: SDS for each HAZMAT, update SOP and spill plan, document waste removal. Containers: check condition and labels, separate incompatibles, keep lids and bungs closed. Kits: spill, first aid and emergency kits near areas, PPE fits and replacements available. Site HAZMAT/HW areas away from billeting, bunkers, ammunition storage, outer perimeter fence lines, dining facilities; HAZMAT near use, HW near generation
entries.use: Daily housekeeping at HAZMAT/HW areas
entries.how: Containment, HAZMAT/HW locations, Environmental documentation, Containers, Kits

entries.desc: All liquid HAZMAT and HW need secondary containment holding 10 percent of total stored or 110 percent of largest container (appendix C wording; chapter 5 text gives 10 percent of total or 100 percent of largest plus freeboard). Seamless, UV-resistant plastic liner; field expedient tarp with sandbags around the perimeter, tarp edges draped over sandbags and folded back into storage area; specialized containment pallets as camp matures; overhead cover to keep rain out. HAZMAT classes: flammable (fuels), corrosive (acids), reactive (explosives), toxic (insecticides) stored separately
entries.use: Liquid HAZMAT/HW containment
entries.how: Hold 10 percent of total or 110 percent of largest container; seamless UV-resistant liner; overhead cover
entries.dim: 10% of total or 110% of largest container (App C); ch 5 says 10% or 100% largest plus ~10% freeboard

entries.desc: Step 1 Protect self and others: alarm/warning, call for help, evacuate nonessential personnel, use SDS PPE, extinguish smoking materials and ignition sources, turn off power if fire possible, ventilate. Step 2 Stop the flow if safe (upright container, close valve; nonsparking tools, avoid metal-to-metal for flammables). Step 3 Contain (drip pans, earthen berms, sandbags, absorbent; divert from storm drains, sewers, waterways). Step 4 Report to chain of command and environmental officer immediately (Figure C-2 format). Step 5 Clean (nonsparking tools for flammables; nonmetallic equipment for corrosives; bag absorbent and soil, place in labeled sturdy container as HW). Step 6 Detailed written report. Step 7 Replace spill equipment. If beyond unit capability: evacuate, inform chain of command, contact local HAZMAT team or fire department. Plan must be posted and rehearsed, updated on significant change
entries.use: Responding to a HAZMAT/HW spill
entries.how: Protect people, stop the flow, contain, report, clean, written report, replace equipment
entries.wn: Personal safety must never be compromised

entries.desc: Lines: 1 date/time; 2 reporting unit, 2A POC, 2B email, 2C phone; 3 DTG of discovery, 3A DTG of spill; 4 material (JP-8, MOGAS, oil, solvent, other, unknown); 5 quantity in gallons, 5A surface (unknown, bare soil, concrete, asphalt), 5B contained (yes/no/unknown); 6 location UTM or 8-digit grid with MGRS zone designator, 6A base camp; 7 cause (accident, enemy fire, negligence); 8 size of area affected in square feet; 9 hazards to environment; 10 hazards to personnel, 10A injuries; 11 actions (remediated, none, unknown); 12 responsible unit/POC/email/phone; 13 assistance required; 14 narrative
entries.use: Reporting a spill
entries.how: Report DTG, unit, POC, material, quantity (gallons), surface, containment, 8-digit grid, cause, area (sq ft), hazards, actions, assistance, narrative
entries.dim: Quantity in gallons; area in square feet; 8-digit grid

entries.desc: Tactical refueling: two nonsparking picks, two nonsparking shovels, several large plastic bags, approximately 10 pounds of absorbent and several small plastic bags. Field maintenance: approximately 25 pounds absorbent, two nonsparking shovels, two brooms, small plastic bags. HAZMAT storage/HW accumulation: approximately 15 pounds absorbent, two nonsparking shovels, two brooms, small bags. HAZMAT/HW transport vehicle: approximately 25 pounds absorbent, two picks, two nonsparking shovels, one broom, small and large plastic bags. Use hydrophobic POL-absorbent near water or in precipitation-prone areas. Units deploy with enough supplies (drums, overpack barrels, absorbent) to contain 10 percent of POL and HAZMAT inventory or the largest container (Table C-1)
entries.use: Stocking spill kits
entries.how: Refueling: 2 picks, 2 shovels, ~10 lb absorbent; maintenance ~25 lb; HW storage ~15 lb; HW transport ~25 lb
entries.dim: Refueling ~10 lb; maintenance ~25 lb; storage ~15 lb; transport ~25 lb; supplies for 10% of inventory or largest container
entries.eq: Absorbent, nonsparking shovels/picks, brooms, bags, overpack drums
entries.src: TM 3-34.56 para C-13 to C-17, C-22, Table C-1

entries.n: Spill cleanup: flammable and combustible organic liquids
entries.desc: Keep away from heat, spark, flame. Dike with sawdust or solid absorbent; use foam (AFFF) if available and pump free liquid with intrinsically safe pump; otherwise absorb with sawdust, cat litter, soil. Scoop with nonsparking shovel into metal or plastic drum. Vapors heavier than air collect low, flashback risk. PPE: rubber/neoprene gauntlet gloves 46 cm (18 in.) long, apron, rubber high-top shoes or overshoes, disposable coveralls, protective mask, face shield when no mask. Fire: CO2 or dry-chemical extinguisher; cool nearby drums with water stream. Exposure: fresh air, first aid, remove contaminated clothing, wash skin 15 minutes under emergency shower, flush eyes 15 minutes, take to medical facility, tell doctor the chemical
entries.use: Fuel/solvent spills
entries.how: Keep away from ignition, dike with sawdust or absorbent, pump free liquid or absorb, scoop with nonsparking shovel, 15 minutes of flushing for exposure
entries.dim: Gauntlet gloves 46 cm (18 in.); wash/flush 15 minutes

entries.n: Spill cleanup: acids (one gallon or less)
entries.desc: pH ranges: 0-4 acidic, 4-6 slightly acidic, 6-8 neutral, 8-10 slightly basic, 10-14 basic. Small amount (a gallon or less) can be neutralized: stay upwind; dike with solid absorbent, socks or pads; do not add water to acid; cover with sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) and test with pH paper until pH 6-8; add sawdust, clay or dry sweep to cover; scoop with long-handled nonsparking shovel; collect in plastic or rubber containers. PPE: gauntlet gloves 46 cm (18 in.), apron, rubber high-top shoes, long-sleeve shirt, protective mask, face shield. Dry chemical or CO2 extinguishers. Exposure: wash skin and flush eyes 15 minutes. Large acid spill: request trained responders; respirators only for trained, pulmonary-fit-tested, fit-tested personnel
entries.use: Small acid spills
entries.how: Stay upwind, dike, never add water to acid, neutralize with sodium bicarbonate to pH 6-8, scoop with long nonsparking shovel
entries.dim: Spill 1 gal or less; neutralize to pH 6-8; 15 minute flush
entries.eq: Sodium bicarbonate, pH paper, absorbent, PPE
entries.wn: Large spill: call trained responders

entries.n: Spill cleanup: bases (one gallon or less)
entries.desc: Some strong bases (e.g., sodium hydroxide) react violently with water; review SDS; keep base-specific spill kit. Large liquid spill: evacuate and request trained responders. Small (a gallon or less): stay upwind and away from low areas; dike with sawdust, vermiculite or clay; neutralize liquid with weak acid (acetic acid or dilute hydrochloric acid); for solids/powders/pellets containerize as much as possible then add water and test pH 6-8; scoop with long nonsparking shovel into color-coded labeled plastic or rubber container. PPE: gauntlet gloves 46 cm (18 in.), long-sleeve shirt, apron, rubber boots, disposable coveralls, face shield, respirator with appropriate cartridges for mists/fumes. Extinguishers: water spray, dry chemical or CO2. Wash 15 minutes
entries.use: Small base/alkali spills
entries.how: Dike with sawdust/vermiculite/clay, neutralize with weak acid to pH 6-8, beware slippery floor and violent reaction of strong bases with water
entries.dim: Spill 1 gal or less; target pH 6-8; 15 minute flush
entries.eq: Weak acid, pH paper, absorbent, PPE
entries.wn: Spilled bases are very slippery

entries.desc: Flash point: flammable liquids have flash point at or below 140 F; combustible liquids at or above 141 F; protect storage from heat in desert climates. Explosive limits (LEL/UEL) in volume percent at 25 C. Vapor density greater than 1.0 (air = 1.0) settles low and can flash back. Specific gravity less than 1.0 floats on water (boom/absorbent placement). pH: below 7 acid, above 7 base; do not store acids and bases together. Boiling point: high-boiling liquids enter mainly by skin contact; low-boiling by inhalation. SDS has 16 sections (Table E-1). SDSs must be available in English and relevant local languages; reviewed periodically; retained for turn-in
entries.use: Using an SDS for storage and spill decisions
entries.how: Flammable liquid flash point <=140 F; combustible >=141 F; check pH, vapor density, specific gravity
entries.dim: Flammable <=140 F; combustible >=141 F; LEL/UEL at 25 C; air density = 1.0; water SG = 1.0
entries.src: TM 3-34.56 para E-3, E-4, E-6, Table E-1

entries.desc: EBS (DD Form 2993 checklist and DD Form 2994 report): during planning/predeployment, documents pre-occupation conditions. ECR: during operation as needed; changes and incidents, archived with EBS. Environmental records: appointment orders, inspections, training, lab results, spill reports, corrective actions. ESCS (DD Form 2995) done three times: initial at transfer/closure notification, preliminary 30 days prior, final after correcting preliminary findings and the Environmental Corrective Action Plan. Environmental Corrective Action Plan after initial ESCS, updated after preliminary. ESCR at transfer/closure after all corrective actions. Transition to enduring location generally takes 90-365 days
entries.use: Documenting a camp from start to finish
entries.how: EBS at planning, ECRs during occupation, ESCS at notification, 30 days before, and final; ESCR at closure
entries.dim: Transition 90-365 days; ESCS initial, 30 days prior, final
entries.src: TM 3-34.56 para F-5, Appendix F intro

entries.n: Base camp closure waste tasks checklist
entries.desc: Major tasks: mitigate environmental effects (close ranges, clean up HAZMAT/HW/POL spills); remove force protection (berms, fighting positions, wire, barriers); set up and close equipment decontamination sites; close maintenance facilities and washracks; close all waste management facilities (solid, hazardous, medical, wastewater, special); contact CCDR staff for HAZMAT/HW removal guidance; disposition of reusables/recyclables; package, inventory, label and turn in HW; terminate waste contracts and remove contractor equipment; empty HW container turn-in; remove fuel bladders and secondary containment liners; dispose of deconstruction waste; close incinerators, landfills, recycling, composting, land farming; shutdown of water purification systems, wastewater and brine lagoon (water survey); wastewater treatment systems; above- and underground storage tanks; close and mark latrines, soakage pits, landfills, trash burial sites, septic systems and record locations. Record all grid coordinates and archive digital photos of each waste site for the ESCR. Equipment must be decontaminated before transfer or transport. Plan the abandonment/destruction case (evacuation routes, rally points, accountability, sensitive items)
entries.use: Closing or transferring a base camp
entries.how: Close and mark latrines, soakage pits, landfills, trash burial sites, septic; record grids; photograph; follow HN agreements

disciplines.desc: Earthmoving and earthwork, roads, airfields, and heliports.

mans.name: TM 3-34.48-1
mans.syn: Design of theater-of-operations roads: geometric design, drainage, soils and CBR, base and surface courses, and construction standards. It provides the criteria and dimensions for building expedient roads and heliports.

mans.name: TM 3-34.62
mans.syn: Operating earthmoving equipment and planning earthwork — excavation, hauling, grading, and compaction. It covers equipment capabilities, production-rate estimation, and soil volume (swell and shrinkage) factors.

disciplines.desc: Structures built up from the ground — concrete, masonry, and carpentry.

mans.name: TM 3-34.44
mans.syn: How to mix, place, finish, and cure concrete and how to build with brick, block, and stone. It includes mix designs and proportions, reinforcement, formwork, and masonry methods.

mans.name: TM 3-34.47
mans.syn: Military carpentry fundamentals — tools, lumber, and fasteners through wall, floor, and roof framing, forms, and field structures. It gives the standard member sizes, spacing, and nailing used in the field.

disciplines.desc: Planning, estimating, surveying, project control, and base support.

mans.name: FM 3-34
mans.syn: The Army’s capstone engineer doctrine: the three engineer disciplines (combat, general, geospatial), the lines of engineer support, how engineer forces are organized, and how engineer work is planned and sustained.

mans.name: TM 3-34.41
mans.syn: How to estimate time, materials, equipment, and manpower for a construction project. It provides production rates, conversion and loss factors, and the method to build a bill of materials and a work estimate.

mans.name: TM 3-34.42
mans.syn: Managing a military construction project from planning through turnover — scheduling, resources, site management, quality control, and safety. It covers the tools and reports used to plan, track, and close out a project.

mans.name: TM 3-34.55
mans.syn: Field surveying for construction: distance, leveling, angles, and traverse; grade and alignment layout; and setting stakes. It covers the instruments, procedures, tolerances, and earthwork computations.

mans.name: TM 3-34.56
mans.syn: Planning and managing solid and liquid waste at deployed base camps — collection, storage, treatment, and disposal. It covers field-expedient methods, waste streams, and environmental considerations.
